[Section heading] The Sin and the Transgression

As for sin (al-ithm) and transgression (al-'udwan), they are companions. God Most High says: ﴿Cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and transgression﴾.

When each of them is mentioned alone, it includes the other. Every sin is a transgression, since it is doing what God has forbidden or leaving what God has commanded, and so it is a transgression against His command and His prohibition. And every transgression is a sin, for its doer incurs sin by it. But when the two are mentioned together, they are two different things, according to their object and their description.

Sin (al-ithm) is what is forbidden in its very kind, such as lying, fornication, drinking wine, and the like. Transgression (al-'udwan) is what is forbidden in its measure and excess.

Transgression, then, is going beyond what is permitted to the forbidden measure and excess, such as overstepping in taking one's right from the one who owes it, whether by encroaching on his property, his body, or his honour. If he seizes a piece of wood from him, he will not accept in return anything but his house; if he destroys something of his, he destroys many times its value; if he says a word about him, he says many times as much about him. All of this is transgression and violation of justice.

This transgression is of two kinds: transgression against the right of God, and transgression against the right of the servant. Transgression against the right of God is like going beyond what God has permitted him of lawful intercourse with wives and slave-women to what He has forbidden other than them, as God says: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 5].

Likewise, when a specific quantity is permitted to him and he exceeds it to more than that, it is transgression. For example, one who is permitted to swallow a morsel stuck in the throat with a sip of wine, yet takes the entire cup; or one who is permitted a look for the purpose of proposal, appraisal, testimony, dealing, or treatment, yet lets the reins of his glance loose in the fields of the beauties of what is looked at, and lets the gaze of his eye roam in those gardens and flowers, thus exceeding what is permitted to the forbidden measure, and circling around the protected, guarded sanctuary. So he becomes one with a bewildered sight and a heart flying from its place. He sends his glance as a scout to bring him news, and it becomes entangled with him and settles in those tents. Then he sends the heart after its traces, and he does not perceive until he is a captive hobbling in his fetters among those tents. The glances of his eye do not cease until he thrashes among them slain, and the swords of those eyelids do not stop striking him until they have thrown him down in a fall. This is the peril of transgression, and what lies ahead of it is greater and more dangerous. This is the loss of deprivation, and what he is deprived of, namely the reward of one who lowers his gaze for God, the Mighty and Majestic, is more exalted and greater. The eye journeyed through the deserts of the beauties of what it looked upon, and gained nothing but the harm of the journey. He gambled with his soul in riding that wilderness, and did not know that the one who rides it is in the greatest danger! What a journey this is, in which the traveler does not reach what he intended, and does not lay down his staff from his shoulder, until the road is cut off for him, and watchers sit for him at every pass and narrow place. He cannot return to his homeland, nor is there any way for him to go or come back. He sees the scorching heat of noon from afar and thinks it is cool drink ﴿until when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full, and God is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

He becomes certain that he had been deceived by the glitter of the mirage. By God, this humiliation and that pleasure are not equal in value, so that the knowing expert would buy one with the other, nor are they close in benefit, so that the discerning person would be perplexed between them. But there is a veil over the eyes, so they do not distinguish between the places of safety and the places of stumbling, and the hearts, under the coverings of heedlessness, lie asleep upon the beds of delusion ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46].

Among the examples of transgression is exceeding what is permitted of carrion in a state of necessity to what is not permitted of it, either by eating to satiety, whereas it was permitted to him only to keep himself alive, according to one of the two opinions in the school of Ahmad, al-Shafi'i, and Abu Hanifa.

Malik permitted him to eat to satiety and to take provision when he needs it. So if he becomes independent of it and eats it while protecting his wealth, and out of stinginess about buying slaughtered meat or the like, then eating it is transgression. God says: ﴿But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then there is no sin upon him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 173]. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: he does not eat it without necessity, nor exceed his satisfaction. It was said: "neither desiring" means not seeking it while he finds other food; "nor transgressing" means not going beyond the limit set for him concerning it, by eating until he is satisfied, but only to keep himself alive. Muqatil said: not regarding it as lawful, nor taking provision from it.

It was also said: he should not rebel by exceeding the limit set for him regarding it, nor transgress by falling short of taking it until he perishes, for then he has transgressed God's limit either by exceeding it or by falling short of it. This one is sinful and that one is sinful. Masruq said: whoever is compelled to eat carrion, blood, or pork, and does not eat or drink until he dies, enters the Fire. This is the more correct of the two opinions regarding the verse. Ibn 'Abbas and his companions and al-Shafi'i said: "neither desiring nor transgressing" means not rebelling against the ruler nor transgressing in one's journey, so the journey is not a journey of disobedience, and on this basis they held that one who is disobedient by his journey does not take the concessions.

The first opinion is more correct for ten reasons, which is not the place to mention. The verse does not address travel either by negation or affirmation, nor the rebellion against the imam, nor is it specific to that, nor was it sent down for it. It is general concerning the resident and the traveler. And the rebellion and transgression in it return to the eating that is the object of the prohibition, not to a matter external to it that has no connection to eating. Also, a parallel to this is His saying in the other verse: ﴿But whoever is compelled by severe hunger, without inclining toward sin﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3]. So this is the one who rebels and transgresses, and the one "inclining toward sin" is the one who leans toward the forbidden measure of eating it, and this is the condition without which it is not permitted to him. Also, it was only permitted out of necessity, so the permission is limited by its measure, and He informed them that exceeding it is rebellion, transgression, and sin, so the permission granted by necessity does not become a cause for its being made lawful. And God knows best.

Sin (al-ithm) and transgression (al-'udwan) are the same as the sin (al-ithm) and rebellion (al-baghy) mentioned in Surat al-A'raf, although rebellion is more commonly used regarding the rights of people and domineering over them.

On this basis, when rebellion (al-baghy) is mentioned together with transgression (al-'udwan), rebellion is their oppression by a forbidden kind, such as theft, lying, slander, and initiating harm, while transgression is exceeding the right in exacting it beyond what is due. So rebellion and transgression regarding people are like sin and transgression regarding the limits of God.

Here there are four matters: a right of God and a limit set for it, and a right of His servants and a limit set for it. Rebellion, transgression, and injustice are going beyond the two limits to what lies beyond them, or falling short of them, so one does not reach them.

(Benefit)

The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "If I had known from my affair what I came to know later, I would not have brought the offering animals, and I would have made it a 'umrah (tamattu')."

There is no regret in it over a better act of worship than what he performed, for God would not have chosen for him anything but the best and highest of rites. Rather, it was out of love for uniting the hearts of his companions, agreeing with them, and comforting their souls, that he should act as they did. He wished that he had taken leave as they had taken leave, but the driving of the offering animals prevented him. Accordingly, God Most High had chosen for him the best of rites through his action, and granted him what he wished of agreement with his companions and the union of their hearts through his intention and desire, so He combined for him both matters. This is what is fitting for him, may God's blessings and peace be upon him.

(Section)

When one contemplates the dazzling wisdom in this upright religion, the Hanif creed and the Muhammadan law, whose perfection words cannot reach and whose beauty description cannot grasp, and which the minds of the wise could not propose even if they were combined and were the most perfect mind of one man, it suffices the perfect and excellent intellects that they perceive its beauty, bear witness to its excellence, and recognize that the world has never been visited by a law more perfect, more majestic, or greater than it.

It is itself the witness and the witnessed-to, the proof and the one for whom proof is given, the claim and the demonstration. Even if the Messenger had brought no proof for it, it would have sufficed as a proof, a sign, and a witness that it is from Allah. All of it bears witness to Him for perfect knowledge, perfect wisdom, vast mercy, benevolence and kindness, comprehensive knowledge of the unseen and the witnessed, and knowledge of beginnings and ends. It is among the greatest blessings Allah has bestowed upon His servants. He has bestowed upon them no blessing greater than guiding them to it, making them of its people, and among those whom He chose for it. Therefore He conferred favour upon His servants by guiding them to it, saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they had been in clear error﴾.

He also said, informing His servants and reminding them of His great blessing upon them, and calling for their gratitude for making them of its people: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾, the verse.

Consider how He described the religion He chose for them as complete, and the blessing He bestowed upon them as full, indicating that in the religion there is no deficiency, no defect, no flaw, and nothing outside wisdom in any respect, but rather it is perfect in its goodness and majesty. And He described the blessing as complete, indicating its permanence and continuity, and that He will not strip them of it after having given it to them, but will complete it for them with permanence in this world and in the abode of settlement.

Consider the fine pairing of completion with blessing, and of perfection with religion, and the attribution of the religion to them, since they are the ones who uphold it and maintain it. And He attributed the blessing to Himself, since He is its patron, its giver, and the One who bestows it upon them; so it is truly a blessing, and they are its recipients.

In the case of perfection He used the preposition lam, which indicates specificity, and that it is something specific to them, not shared with the nations. In the case of completing the blessing He used ʿala, which indicates elevation, encompassing and surrounding. Thus "atmamtu" corresponds to "akmaltu," "ʿalaykum" corresponds to "lakum," and "niʿmati" corresponds to "dinikum." He emphasized this, reinforced it, and added to its confirmation, perfection, and completion of the blessing by His saying: ﴿And I have approved Islam as your religion﴾.

[Section: Divisions of Blessing]

Blessing is of two kinds: absolute blessing (niʿmah muṭlaqah) and restricted blessing (niʿmah muqayyadah).

1. Absolute blessing is that which is connected to eternal happiness, and it is the blessing of Islam and the Sunnah. It is the blessing which Allah, Glorified is He, commanded us to ask Him for in our prayers, that He guide us to the path of its people and of those whom He singled out for it and made the people of the Highest Companionship, where He says, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions﴾ [al-Nisa’: 69].

These four categories are the people of this absolute blessing, and its possessors are also those intended by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My blessing upon you, and approved Islam as your religion – so whoever is compelled by severe hunger, not inclining toward sin, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful…﴾. He attributed the religion to them, since they are the ones specially concerned with this upright religion, apart from the rest of the nations. Religion is sometimes attributed to the servant and sometimes attributed to the Lord, so it is said that Islam is the religion of Allah, which He does not accept from anyone other than it.

For this reason it is said in supplication: "O Allah, support Your religion which You sent down from the heaven." Perfection was attributed to the religion and completion to the blessing, with its attribution to Him, because He is its patron and the One who bestows it upon them, while they are a pure locus for His blessings, receiving them. For this reason it is said in the transmitted supplication for the Muslims: "And make them praise You for it, accepting it, and complete it for them."

As for the religion, since they are those who uphold it and act upon it by the success of their Lord, He attributed it to them, saying: ﴿I have perfected for you your religion﴾. Perfection was on the side of the religion and completion on the side of the blessing. Although the two words are close and balanced, there is a subtle difference which appears upon reflection: perfection is more specific to attributes and meanings, and it is also applied to entities and essences, by consideration of their attributes and properties, as the Prophet ﷺ said: ("Many men have attained perfection, but among women none has attained perfection except Maryam daughter of ʿImran, Asiyah daughter of Muzahim, and Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid.").

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz said: "Indeed faith has limits, obligations, sunan, and laws; whoever completes them has completed faith." As for completion (tamam), it occurs in entities and meanings, and the blessings of Allah are entities, attributes, and meanings.

As for His religion, it is His law, comprising His command, His prohibition, and what He loves. Thus attributing perfection to the religion and completion to the blessing is the better arrangement, just as attributing the religion to them and the blessing to Him is better. The intent is that this blessing is the absolute blessing, which is specific to the believers. If it is said that Allah has no blessing upon the disbeliever in this sense, then that is correct.

The second blessing is the restricted blessing, like the blessing of health, wealth, bodily well-being, extended status, abundance of children, a good wife, and the like. This blessing is shared between the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever. If it is said that Allah has a blessing upon the disbeliever in this sense, that is true. Thus affirmation and negation can only be applied absolutely in one respect: restricted blessings, since they are a means of gradual drawing-down (istidraj) for the disbeliever and their outcome is punishment and misery, are as if they were not blessings but rather a trial, as Allah Exalted named them in His Book. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him and honours him and bestows favour upon him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." No! …﴾ [al-Fajr: 15-16], the verse. That is: not everyone whom I have honoured and favoured in this world have I favoured in truth; rather that was a trial and test from Me for him. Nor does everyone whose provision I have restricted, giving him according to his need without bounty, mean that I have humiliated him. Rather I test My servant with blessings as I test him with calamities.

If it is said: how does this meaning fit with His saying: ﴿and honoured him and favoured him﴾ [al-Fajr: 15], affirming honour, and then He denied his saying: ﴿My Lord has honoured me﴾ [al-Fajr: 15], and said: "No!" That is, that is not honour from Me, but rather a trial? So it seems He affirmed honour for him and negated it?

It is said: the honour affirmed is other than the honour negated; both are of the kind of absolute and restricted blessing. This restricted honour does not necessitate that its possessor is among the people of absolute honour.

Likewise, if it is said that Allah bestowed upon the disbeliever an absolute blessing, but he rejected the blessing of Allah and exchanged it, he is like one who is given what he cannot live by, and then throws it into the sea, as Allah says: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]. And He says: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17]. His guidance of them was a blessing from Him upon them, but they exchanged His blessing and preferred misguidance over it. This is the decisive resolution of the question: Does Allah have a blessing upon the disbeliever or not?

Most of people's disagreement arises from two sources: first, the homonymy and ambiguity of terms; second, the matter of absolute and detailed (specification).

(Section)

On the fact that absolute blessing is that in which one truly rejoices, together with a statement of the rank of the Sunnah and its follower:

This absolute blessing is that in which one truly rejoices, and rejoicing in it is among what Allah loves and approves, and He does not love those who rejoice. Allah Exalted says: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ [Yunus: 58].

The sayings of the early scholars (salaf) have revolved around the view that the bounty of Allah and His mercy are Islam and the Sunnah. According to the life of the heart, its joy in these is measured: the more firmly rooted it is in them, the greater its joy becomes, to the extent that the heart dances with joy when it touches the spirit of the Sunnah, though it is the most sorrowful of people, and it is filled with security though it is the most fearful of people.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 5, verse 4:

Were it not for the distinction of knowledge and teaching and their nobility, the hunt of a trained dog and that of an ignorant one would be equal.

(Section)

You have trained your dog, so it leaves aside its appetite for what it has caught, out of respect for your favour and fear of your power. And how many a teacher of the Sharia has taught you, yet you do not accept.

The hunt of the ignorant one is forbidden, and so is that of the one who keeps it for himself. How, then, do you think of the ignorant one whose deeds are for the sake of his own desire?!

He combines in himself the intellect of an angel, the appetite of a beast, and the desire of Satan, and you are dominated by one of these three. If your appetite and desire prevail, you rise above the rank of an angel; and if your desire and appetite overcome you, you fall below the rank of a dog.

When the dog hunts for its master, its catch is made lawful; but when it keeps the prey for itself, what it has caught is forbidden.

[Section: The wisdom in washing the parts of wudu' (ablution)]

As for His making it obligatory to wash the places from which wind did not emerge, and dropping the washing of the place from which it did emerge, how perfectly this fits wisdom, and how strongly it accords with the innate nature (fitrah). The essence of the objection is: why is wudu' prescribed for these outward limbs and not for the inner part of the rectum, when the inner part of the rectum deserves wudu' more than the face, the hands and the feet? This is an inverted question from an upside-down heart. Among the excellences of the Sharia is that wudu' was prescribed for the outward, exposed limbs, and that the most deserving of it is the one that leads and precedes them in mention and in action, which is the face, whose cleanliness and radiance are a sign of the cleanliness of the heart. After it come the two hands, which are the instruments of grasping, taking and seizing, so they are the most deserving of cleanliness and purity after the face. Since the head is the gathering place of the senses and the highest and most noble part of the body, it deserved cleansing. But if washing it had been prescribed in wudu', the hardship would have been great and the trial severe, so He prescribed wiping the whole of it and placed that in the position of washing it, as a lightening and a mercy, just as He placed wiping over the two leather socks (khuffayn) in the position of washing the two feet.

Perhaps someone will say: what does wiping the head and the feet achieve in terms of washing and cleanliness? This speaker does not know that touching a limb with water in obedience to the command of Allah, in submission to Him and in worship, affects its cleanliness and purity in a way that washing it with water and lote-leaves without this intention does not. Judgment on this is referred to sound taste and upright natural disposition. Just as rubbing the face with dust in obedience to the One who commands, in submission and servitude, gives it radiance, cleanliness and brightness that appear on its surface to those who look at it.

Since the two feet often touch the ground and come into contact with filth that the other limbs do not come into contact with, they deserved washing more. Whoever suffices with wiping them without any barrier has not been granted understanding of what Allah and His Messenger intended.

This is the reason these limbs are singled out for wudu' from among the rest, as far as what is perceived is concerned. As for the meaning, these limbs are the instruments of actions by which the servant carries out what he wishes to do, and by which Allah, glorified is He, is disobeyed or obeyed. The hand seizes, the foot walks, the eye looks, the ear hears, the tongue speaks. So in washing these limbs, in obedience to the command of Allah and in upholding His worship, there is what requires the removal of the stain and filth of disobedience that has reached them.

The Lawgiver (ﷺ) has indicated this very meaning when he said in the authentic hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, from 'Amr ibn 'Abasah, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me about wudu'.' He said: 'None of you approaches his wudu', then rinses his mouth and snuffs water into his nose and blows it out, but the sins of his face fall away from the edges of his beard along with the water. Then he washes his hands up to the elbows, and the sins of his hands fall away from his fingertips along with the water. Then he wipes his head, and the sins of his head fall away from the ends of his hair along with the water. Then he washes his feet up to the ankles, and the sins of his feet fall away from his toes along with the water. If he then stands and prays, praising Allah, extolling Him and glorifying Him with what He is worthy of, and empties his heart for Allah, he will depart from his sin as on the day his mother bore him.'"

In Sahih Muslim also, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Muslim servant - or the believer - performs wudu' and washes his face, every sin that he looked at with his eyes goes out of his face with the water - or with the last drop of water. When he washes his hands, every sin that his hands seized goes out of his hands with the water - or with the last drop of water. When he washes his feet, every sin that his feet walked to goes out with the water - or with the last drop of water - until he comes out pure of sins."

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'Two men of my Ummah: one of them gets up at night, struggling with himself to purify himself, and he has knots upon him, so he performs wudu'. When he washes his hands, a knot is untied; when he washes his face, a knot is untied; when he wipes his head, a knot is untied; when he washes his feet, a knot is untied. Then the Lord, mighty and majestic, says to those behind the veil: 'Look at this servant of Mine who struggles with himself. Whatever My servant asks Me, it is his.'"

In it also, from Abu Umamah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever stands to his wudu' intending prayer, then washes his palms, his sin descends from his palms with the first drop. When he rinses his mouth, snuffs water into his nose and blows it out, his sin descends from his tongue and lips with the first drop. When he washes his face, his sin descends from his hearing and sight with the first drop. When he washes his hands up to the elbows and his feet up to the ankles, he is safe from every sin that is his, and from every sin as on the day his mother bore him. When he stands for prayer, Allah raises his rank by it; and if he sits, he sits in safety."

In it also: the purpose of rinsing the mouth is the same as the purpose of washing the face and hands, and the tongue and lips need washing just as the rest of the limbs do. So whoever is more perverted of heart, more corrupt of natural disposition, and more invalid in analogy than the one who says that washing the inner part of the rectum is more deserving than washing these limbs, and that the Lawgiver distinguished between two alike? Besides this, washing these limbs accompanied by the intention of worship to Allah brings expansion of the heart and its strength, breadth of chest, joy of soul, and vigour of the limbs. Thus they were distinguished from the other limbs by what made their washing obligatory rather than that of others. And success is from Allah.

[Section: The wisdom in wudu' being broken by touching one's private part and not other limbs]

As for his saying: "Wudu' is broken by touching the private part and not the other limbs, nor by touching excrement or urine," there is no doubt that it has been authentically established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he commanded wudu' after touching the private part, and that the opposite was also narrated from him, and that he was asked about it and said to the questioner: "Is it not but a part of your body?" It has been said that this report is not authentic; it has been said that it is abrogated (mansukh) by a later ruling; and it has been said that it is definitive (muhkam), indicating non-obligation, while the hadith of the command indicates recommendation. So these are three positions held by people on this matter.

The questioner's objection is built on the authenticity of the hadith of the command to perform wudu' and that it is obligatory. We answer him on this assumption, and we say: this is part of the perfection of the Sharia and the completeness of its excellences. Touching the private part, which is in the usual position of erection, and the erection arising from touching is in the usual position of the emission of madhi (pre-seminal fluid) which one may not notice; so this usual condition was placed in the position of the reality because of its hiddenness and frequent occurrence, just as sleep was placed in the position of the breaking of wind, and just as touching a woman with desire was placed in the position of ritual impurity (hadath).

Also, touching the private part causes the heat of desire to spread and surge through the body, and wudu' extinguishes that heat, and this is observed by the senses. And wudu' was not from touching it because it is impure, nor because it is the channel of impurity, so that the questioner could raise touching excrement and urine. His claim that touching the private part is equivalent to touching the nose is among the most false claims and most invalid analogies. And success is from Allah.

[Section: The wisdom in combining water and dust in the rule of purification]

As for His combining water and dust in purification, by Allah, how excellent is this combination, how subtle, and how closely it attaches to sound minds and upright natural dispositions! Allah, glorified is He, has established brotherhood between water and dust by decree and by Sharia. He gathered them and created from them Adam and his descendants, so they became the two parents of our parents and their offspring. He made from them the life of every living creature, and brought forth from them the sustenance of beasts, people and livestock. They are the most widely existent of things and the easiest to obtain. Rubbing the face in dust for Allah is among the things most beloved to Him. And since the establishing of this brotherhood between them by decree is the firmest and strongest bond, the establishing of brotherhood between them by Sharia is the finest and most sound bond. "So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds" (Al-Jathiyah: 36). "And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise" (Al-Jathiyah: 37).

(Benefit: On the precedence of washing the face)

As for the precedence of washing the face, then the hand, then wiping the head, then the feet in wudu': those who say that this order is obligatory are al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with them both. Whoever agrees with them holds that the verse required this order as an obligation, due to several indications.

The first: He placed a wiped limb between two washed limbs and separated a counterpart from its counterpart. Had the unrestricted combination been intended, it would have been appropriate to mention the washed limbs in sequence, followed by the wiped one. When He deviated from this, it showed that their order as He mentioned it is obligatory.

The second: these acts are parts of a single act commanded, which is wudu', so the conjunction "wa" (and) entered to link its parts to one another, and a single act is achieved through the linking of its parts to one another. So "wa" entered between the parts for linking, and thus it conveyed order, since that is the linking mentioned in the verse. It does not follow that because it does not convey order between acts that have no connection, such as "Establish prayer and give zakah," it must not convey order between parts of one act that are linked to one another. Reflect on this point and its subtlety. This is one of the three opinions on whether "wa" conveys order, and most of the jurists of usul do not know it or report it. It is the view of Ibn Abi Musa among the companions of Ahmad, and it is perhaps the most preponderant of the opinions.

The third: the Lord, exalted is He, specifically began with the face among all the limbs, so it is obligatory to observe this, and not to disregard and nullify it, so that what Allah regarded is not discarded and what Allah put first is not postponed.

The Prophet (ﷺ) has indicated that what Allah put first should be put first and not postponed. Rather, what Allah put first is put first, and what He put last is put last. When he performed the tawaf between al-Safa and al-Marwah, he began with al-Safa and said: "We begin with what Allah began with." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Malik, and Muslim narrated something similar. In a narration of al-Nasa'i: "Begin with what Allah began with," in the form of a command.

Reflect on his beginning with al-Safa, giving as the reason that Allah began with it, so it is not right to postpone it.

Likewise say those who require the order in wudu': we begin with what Allah began with, it is not permissible to postpone what Allah put first, and it is necessary to begin with what Allah began with.

This is the correct view, because the one who explains Allah's intention, the Prophet (ﷺ), was constant in performing wudu' in order, and all who have transmitted his wudu' agree that he performed it in order, and no one has ever transmitted that he omitted the order even once. If an inverted wudu' had been legislated, he would have performed it at least once in his life to show its permissibility to his Ummah.

Praise be to Allah, this is clear.

(Benefit)

It has been argued that intention is not a condition for the purity of water, because water was created with specific attributes and a nature whose effects do not require intention to be realized. It was created purifying (tahur), created sweet, and created cool and fluid; all of that is its nature and the attribute it was given. Just as intention is not required for water to produce quenching and cooling, so too it is not required for purification. It is clarified by the fact that it was created pure, or purifying, and its purity does not depend on intention; so likewise its purifying quality does not depend on it.

It is further clarified by the fact that its action in the stronger of the two kinds of purity, which is purity from impurity (khabath), does not depend on intention. So the fact that its action in the other purity does not depend on intention is more fitting. We say that it is the stronger of the two purities because its cause and what necessitates it is a sensory matter, a visible filth; and because it has no substitute from dust. Thus its strength has appeared both sensorially and legally.

It is further clarified by his (ﷺ) saying: "Water was created purifying." This is explicit that it was created with this attribute, and "purifying" (tahuran) is in the accusative as a state, meaning created in this state of being purifying. Even if this state is a necessary state, it is like the saying: "Allah created the giraffe with its forelegs longer than its hind legs." So this attribute, which is purifying, was created along with it, whether one intends or not.

The argument from this is close to the argument from His saying: "And We sent down from the sky pure (tahur) water" (Al-Furqan: 48).

It is further clarified that if intention is considered in terms of water flowing over the limbs, that occurs whether one intends or not. If the goal considered is the attainment of freshness and cleanliness, then likewise its attainment does not depend on intention. If it is considered for removing the ritual impurity attached to the limbs, we have already shown that the impurity attached to them is stronger than ritual impurity, and the removal of this stronger thing does not depend on intention, so how much less so the weaker.

It is further clarified that we have seen the Sharia divides the actions of the responsible persons into two kinds: a kind whose intended purpose is achieved by its very occurrence, so intention is not required for its validity, such as paying debts, returning trusts, obligatory maintenance, carrying out prescribed punishments, removing impurities, washing perfume off the one in ihram, the waiting period of separation, and other things. The benefits of these acts are achieved by their existence, arising from their very nature. So when they occur, their benefits are attained, and their validity does not depend on intention.

The second category: that whose purpose and aim are not achieved by the act alone. Its mere outward form, stripped of intention, does not suffice, such as uttering the words of Islam, the talbiyah (the call recited during ihram), the form of tayammum (dry ablution with earth), circumambulating the House (tawaf), running between al-Safa and al-Marwah (sa'y), prayer, i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque), and fasting. Since the removal of impurity (izalat al-khabath) belongs to the first category, its outward act alone was sufficient to achieve its purpose.

We have explained that the purpose of wudu' (ablution) is cleanliness, purity, and the servant standing before his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, in his most perfect condition: his private parts covered, avoiding impurity, with his limbs clean and radiant. This is achieved by performing these acts, whether or not he intends them.

This is clarified by the fact that wudu' is not sought for its own sake but for the sake of something else. What is sought for something else does not need to be intended, because it is a means. Intention is required only for what is sought for its own sake, for that is the true aim. Thus the intention to cover the distance in Hajj or Friday prayer is not obligatory, and validity does not depend on it. Likewise, the intention to buy water, or to buy a slave for the freeing of a captive, or to buy food, is not obligatory, because these are means sought for something other than themselves.

Likewise, wudu' is a means sought for prayer, so it is like the purity of the place and the garments. Intention is required in acts of worship.

This is further clarified by the fact that if intention were required in wudu', it would be required in all the conditions of prayer, such as covering the private parts, removing impurity, and other things. I do not think those who dispute with the people (of this view) can answer these arguments with a satisfying answer. These are their answers in their own path, so refer to them. We do not accept this opinion, but we have not found the arguments of their opponents and their replies to them stronger than these proofs. This is not because the issue is weak on their side, but because the discussion of intention (niyyah) is closely tied to the works of the hearts, to knowing their levels, to their connection with the works of the limbs, to their foundation upon them, and to their influence on them, in soundness and corruption. Intention is the principal, sought-after foundation, while the works of the limbs follow it, complete it, and perfect it. Intention is like the spirit, and action is like the body of the limbs: when the spirit departs, there is death, and likewise action without intention is the movement of a idle person. Therefore, knowing the rulings of the hearts is more important than knowing the rulings of the limbs, for the former is their root, and the rulings of the limbs branch from it.

Likewise, the discussion of this issue cannot be realized until one knows the true nature of intention: whether it belongs to the category of knowledge and perceptions, or to the category of wills and resolutions, or whether its reality is composed of both. As for the notion that it extends and divides into specific letters, with each letter containing a part of the intention, this does not even attain the meaning of intention, let alone enable one to refute the view of his opponent who considers it a requirement.

Likewise, whoever thinks that intention is realized only by the flow of words from the tongue that express it, has not attained its meaning either. Therefore, we must first know its reality, its position among the works of the hearts, and that it is impossible for it to extend or divide, and that words have no role in it at all. One must distinguish between the intention directed at the Worshipped, which is among the requirements and consequences of Islam, indeed its very spirit and reality, without which Allah accepts no deed from a doer at all, and the intention directed at the act itself, about which disagreement has arisen in some matters. Then one recognizes its connection with the act, and how it is intended to distinguish worship (ibadah) from custom (adah), since the two may be identical in form, and they are distinguished only by intention. When intention is absent, the act is customary, not devotional. Customs are not means of drawing near to the Creator of creatures and the Originator of beings. When an act is stripped of intention, it becomes like eating, drinking, and animal sleep, which is not worship in any respect, let alone something commanded, rewarded, punished, praised, or blamed. What is of this nature cannot be prescribed as a means of drawing near to the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted. Therefore, intention is also intended to distinguish the ranks of acts of worship from one another, to distinguish the obligatory from the voluntary, and their ranks from each other. These matters are not realized except through intention, and they have no stability without it at all. They are also desired by the Llégislateur (al-Shari'); indeed, they are the duties of servitude. How can one fulfill the duties of servitude if he does not even consider distinguishing acts of worship from customs, nor distinguishing the ranks of those duties and their stations of servitude? This is impossible by custom, reason, and law. Intention is thus the secret of servitude and its spirit, and its place in the act is the place of the spirit in the body. It is impossible that the works of the hearts should count toward servitude while the spirit is absent; rather, such acts are like a ruined body. This is the meaning of the report transmitted as a statement of Amir al-Mu'minin Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): "There is no deed for one who has no intention, and no reward for one who has no sincere purpose."

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾. He, glory be to Him, forbade that He command His servants except with the worship in which the doer has made his intention sincere for Him. It is well known that sincerity of intention toward the Worshipped is the root of intention for the root of worship. So when He commands them only with an act that is worship, in which the doer has made his intention sincere for his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is known that intention is a part of worship, indeed its spirit, as has been shown, it is known that an act performed without intention is neither worship nor commanded, and its doer is not drawing near to Allah, the Exalted. This is something that admits no dispute.

Among the subtleties of this issue is that one distinguishes between acts that by custom occur only with intention, and acts that may occur with or without intention. The first kind, such as wudu' in which the limbs are washed one after another, can hardly be conceived as occurring without intention. For the knowledge of the doer about what he is doing, and his purpose in it, is intention, and a rational, choosing person does not perform an act except after having conceived and willed it, and that is the reality of intention. Intention is not something external to the doer's conception and purpose for what he wishes to do. From this, the error of those who think that uttering the words contributes to forming the intention becomes clear. When one says, "I intend the noon prayer" or "I intend to lift the ritual impurity (raf' al-hadath)," he is either informing or initiating. If he is informing, then either he informs himself or others. Both are futile, for information benefits only when it conveys to the informed what he did not know. This is impossible when one informs himself. If he informs others of his intention, it is pure futility, not prescribed and not beneficial. It is like informing them of all his other actions, his fasting, prayer, pilgrimage, and zakah, indeed like informing them of his faith, his love, and his hatred. Yet in this kind of information there may be some benefit.

As for informing the followers, the imam, or others of the intention, it is pure futility. It cannot be a initiating act, for words do not bring the intention into existence. Initiating intention is rather bringing its reality into the heart, not initiating the words that indicate it.

It is thus known that uttering it is pure futility. Reflect on this brilliant subtlety. The point is that such ordered acts, which occur only with knowledge and purpose, are necessarily intended. This differs from ghusl, for example, which may be performed for cleaning, cooling, or similar purposes. If its doer does not intend to lift his ritual impurity, it is not intended as such. Likewise, the ordered acts of prayer, each following the other, occur only with intention. If a man tried to pray or perform wudu' without intention, it would be impossible for him, though it may be conceived in the case where he intends to teach another and does not intend worship, or where he prays and performs wudu' under compulsion.

As for a rational, choosing person who knows what he is doing, whose act occurs in accordance with his purpose, this can only be intentional. Intention is purpose itself, but there are two differences between intention and purpose. The first is that purpose relates to the doer's own act and to the act of others, whereas intention relates only to his own act. It is not conceivable for a man to intend another's act, though he can purpose and will it. The second difference is that purpose occurs only with a capable act that the doer intends. Intention, however, may relate to what a person is capable of and what he is incapable of. For this reason, in the hadith of Abu Kabshah al-Anmari, narrated by Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and others, from the Prophet (ﷺ):

"The world belongs to four kinds of people: a servant whom Allah has given wealth and knowledge, so he fears his Lord regarding his wealth, uses it to maintain ties of kinship, and recognizes Allah's right in it; this one is in the best station with Allah. And a servant whom Allah has given knowledge but not wealth, who says, 'If I had wealth, I would act with it as so-and-so does,' so his reward and intention are equal (to that of the first). And a servant whom Allah has given wealth but not knowledge, who wastes it without knowledge; this is the worst station with Allah." Then he said: "And a servant whom Allah has given neither wealth nor knowledge, who says, 'If I had wealth, I would act with it as so-and-so does,' so his intention is (equal to that of the one who acts wrongly), and both are equal in sin."

Thus intention relates to what is capable and what is incapable, unlike purpose and will, which relate neither to what is incapable, whether from the agent's act or from another's act. When the reality of intention and its place within faith and its laws is known, the discussion of this issue, in denial and affirmation, becomes clear, with knowledge and fairness.

(Section)

Reflect on the chapters of the Shari'ah, its means and its ends, and how you find them filled with desired wisdoms and praiseworthy goals for which they were prescribed. Without these, people would be like beasts, or even worse. How much wisdom and benefit there is in purification (taharah) for the heart and body: it gladdens the heart, invigorates the limbs, lightens the burdens that nature imposes, and cleanses the soul of the filth of transgressions. It cleanses the heart, the spirit, and the body. In ghusl from janabah there is additional smoothness and renewal for the body, corresponding to what was dissolved by the janabah, which is among the most beneficial things.

Reflect on the fact that wudu' is performed on the extremities, which are the places of earning and work. It is performed on the face, which contains hearing, sight, speech, smell, and taste, and these are the gates through which all sins and transgressions enter. Then it is performed on the hands, which are its two extremities and wings, with which one grasps, takes, and gives. Then on the two feet, with which one walks and strives. Since washing the head involves greatest hardship and difficulty, wiping was substituted for it, and this becomes an outlet for sins from these places, so that they leave with the drops of water from the hair and the skin, as was established from the Prophet (ﷺ) in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "When the Muslim or believing servant performs wudu' and washes his face, every sin he looked at with his eyes leaves his face with the water, or with the last drop of water. When he washes his hands, every sin his hands seized leaves his hands with the water, or with the last drop. When he washes his feet, every sin his feet walked to leaves with the water, or with the last drop of water, until he comes out pure from sins."

Narrated by Muslim.

In Sahih Muslim also, from Uthman ibn Affan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs wudu' and does it well, his sins leave him until they leave from under his fingernails."

This is among the greatest wisdoms and benefits of wudu'. Those who deny wisdom (nufat al-hikmah) said that it is merely obligation, hardship, and pure toil, with no benefit in it and no wisdom for which it was prescribed. Yet even if there were no benefit and wisdom in it except that it is the mark of this Ummah and its sign on their faces and limbs on the Day of Resurrection, distinct from all other nations, it would suffice. And even if there were no benefit and wisdom in it except that the one performing wudu' purifies his hands with water and his heart with repentance, to prepare himself to enter upon his Lord, to commune with Him, and to stand before Him pure in body, garment, and heart, what greater wisdom, mercy, and benefit could there be than this?

Since desire flows through the entire body, so that beneath every hair there is desire, the ghusl of janabah extends to wherever desire has spread, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beneath every hair is janabah." Therefore one is commanded to let the water reach the root of every hair, to cool the heat of desire, so that the soul becomes calm and at peace in the remembrance of Allah, the recitation of His speech, and standing before Him. By Allah, if Hippocrates and those beneath him had enjoined something like this, their followers would have submitted to them in it and held them in the highest esteem, and they would have displayed as much wisdom and benefit as they could.

Then, since a servant outside of prayer neglects his limbs, letting them loose in the pastures of desires and pleasures, the command of servitude requires him to present all his limbs to his Lord with their portion of servitude. Thus his heart, body, limbs, senses, and powers submit to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, standing before Him, turned wholly toward Him, turning away from all others, repenting of his neglect of Him and of his transgression against His right. Since this is his nature and essence, the prayer is prescribed to renew this bowing to Him and this turning toward Him from time to time, lest the period grow long and he forget his Lord and be entirely cut off from Him. Prayer is among the greatest blessings of Allah upon him and the finest of the gifts He has bestowed upon him. Yet those who deny wisdom insisted on making it a burden, toil, and labor, with no wisdom or benefit whatsoever, but merely compulsion and will. By this door they have opened the way to treat the entire Shari'ah from beginning to end in this manner. Derive from what is apparent to you what is hidden from you. Perhaps the wisdom in what you do not know is greater than what you know, for what you know is according to your intellect and understanding, while what is hidden from you is beyond your intellect and understanding. If we were to trace the details of this, it would fill several volumes, so one should be content with a brief proof. And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

As for His making the hearts hard, the Exalted said: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of.﴾

Qaswah (hardness) means strength and firmness in anything. It is said: "a hard stone" (ḥajar qāsin) and "a hard land" (arḍ qāsiyah) that produces nothing. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "qāsiyah ʿan al-īmān" (hard toward faith).

al-Ḥasan said: "ṭubiʿa ʿalayhā" (it was sealed upon).

Hearts are of three kinds: a hard heart, which is dry and firm, not accepting the form of truth and not being impressed by it; its opposite is the soft, cohesive heart, which is sound and free of disease, accepting the form of truth through its softness and retaining it through its cohesiveness. This is unlike the diseased heart, which does not retain what is impressed upon it because of its slipperiness and looseness, like a liquid: when you impress something into it, it takes the form because of its softness, but its looseness prevents it from holding that form. So the best of hearts is the firm, pure, soft heart: it sees the truth through its purity, accepts it through its softness, and retains it through its firmness.

In the Musnad and others, it is related from the Prophet ﷺ: "The hearts are the vessels of Allah on His earth, so the dearest of them to Him are the firmest, the softest and the purest."

The Exalted has mentioned the kinds of hearts in His saying: ﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened. Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension. And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, and their hearts humbly submit to it.﴾

He mentioned the diseased heart, which is the weak, loosened heart in which the form of truth does not settle; the hard heart, which is dry and does not accept it nor is it impressed by it; and these two hearts are wretched and punished. Then He mentioned the humble heart, which is at rest with it, and which benefits from the Qur'an and is purified by it.

al-Kalbi said: "fa-takhbita lahu qulūbuhum" means "their hearts are softened so that they become tender toward the Qur'an."

(Section)

Among their slanders against the prophets is what they attribute to the text of the Torah.

When Allah destroyed the people of Lot for their corruption, and saved Lot with only his two daughters, the two daughters thought the earth had been emptied of men who could give them offspring. The elder said to the younger: "Our father is an old man, and there is no man left on earth who would come to us in the way of mankind. Come, let us make our father drink wine and lie with him, that we may preserve offspring from our father." So they did this, by their claim.

They attributed to the Prophet Lot ʿalayhi al-salām that he became drunk, so that he did not recognize his daughters, then he had intercourse with them and they conceived while he did not know them. One of them bore a son whom she named "Moab," meaning "from the father." The other named her son "Ben-Ammi," meaning "he is from her tribe."

Some of them have answered this by saying that it occurred before the Torah was revealed, so intermarriage among relatives was not yet forbidden. But the Torah refutes them:

In it, "Abraham the Friend feared in that era that the Egyptians would kill him out of envy for his wife Sarah, so he concealed their marriage and said: 'She is my sister,' knowing that if he said that, no path would remain for suspicions regarding them."

This is the clearest proof that the prohibition of marrying a sister was established in that time. So what do you think of marrying a daughter, which was not legislated even in the time of Adam ʿalayhi al-salām?

They also have, in the Torah in their hands, a story more wondrous than this:

That Judah son of Jacob, the prophet, married his eldest son to a woman called "Tamar," and he used to approach her from behind, so God the Exalted became angry at his deed and caused him to die. Then Judah married her to his other son, and whenever he entered upon her he would spill on the ground, knowing that if she bore a child, the first child would be called by the name of his brother and attributed to his brother. God the Exalted disliked this deed of his, so He caused him to die also. Then Judah ordered her to return to her father's house until his son grew up, matured in intellect, fearing that what had happened to his two brothers might befall him. So she remained in her father's house. Then Judah's wife died, and he went up to a place called Manath to shear his sheep. When the woman Tamar was informed of her father-in-law's going up to the place, she dressed in the garb of prostitutes and sat at a lookout on his road, knowing his lust. When he passed by her, he took her to be a prostitute and solicited her, and she demanded a payment; he promised her a young goat, and he left with her his staff and his seal, and he lay with her, and she conceived by him.

When Judah was informed that his daughter-in-law had conceived from fornication, he gave the order for her to be burned. So she sent to him his seal and his staff, and said: "By the owner of these I am pregnant." He said: "You have spoken the truth, and it is from me." He excused himself by saying that he had not known her, and he did not consider it lawful to return to her or to give her to his son. She conceived from this fornication with Perez. They said: "From his offspring was the Prophet David."

In this there is the attribution of fornication and disbelief to the house of prophethood, approaching what they attributed to Lot ʿalayhi al-salām. All of this is in their own books and in the text of their scripture. They make this a lineage for David and Solomon ʿalayhima al-salām, and for their expected messiah.

Among the wonders: they call the Muslims illegitimate children, and name them "mamzerim," whose singular is "mamzer," which is the term for an illegitimate child, because in their law, if a husband takes back his wife after she has married another man, their children are illegitimate.

They claim that what the law of Islam brought of this is among the fabrications of ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, intended to make the children of Muslims "mamzerim," by their claim.

They say: Muhammad ﷺ had seen dreams indicating that he would be a man of dominion, so he travelled to Syria on trade for Khadijah. He met the rabbis of the Jews and related to them his dreams, and they knew that he would be a man of dominion, so they had ʿAbdullah ibn Salam accompany him. He studied with him the sciences and jurisprudence of the Torah for a period. They attributed the eloquence and inimitability that are in the Qur'an to ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, and that among what ʿAbdullah ibn Salam established was that a wife is not lawful to a man who divorced her three times unless another man marries her, so as to make the children of Muslims "mamzerim," illegitimate.

There is no doubt that such slander deceives many of their common folk.

Allah has appointed for every falsehood and slander carriers, just as truth has carriers, and beyond this slander there is no slander.

It is not strange from a people who have defamed their worshipped deity, attributing to Him what is not befitting His greatness and majesty, and who attributed to His prophets what is not befitting them, hurling grave charges at them, that they should attribute to Muhammad ﷺ, may Allah exalt, honour and magnify him and his family, such things. Their enmity toward them, his battles against them, his expelling them from their homes and property, and his taking captive their offspring and women, is well known and not unknown.

This wrathful people have attributed to ʿIsa ibn Maryam that he was a sorcerer, born of fornication, and they attributed his mother to immorality.

They attributed to Lot that he had intercourse with his two daughters and fathered children by them while he was drunk from wine.

They attributed to Solomon ʿalayhi al-salām that he was a sorcerer king, and his father, in their view, was a messiah king.

They attributed to Joseph ʿalayhi al-salām that he loosened the drawstring of his trousers and the drawstring of his mistress's trousers, and that he sat with her in the manner of a man with his wife, and that the wall split open for him and he saw his father Jacob ʿalayhi al-salām biting his fingers, so he did not rise until Gabriel ʿalayhi al-salām descended and said: "O Joseph, will you be among the fornicators, when you are counted with Allah among the prophets?" Then he rose at that point.

It is known that refraining from immorality because of this carries no praise, for the most depraved of people, if he saw this, would flee and abandon the immorality.

Among them are those who claim that the Messiah was among the scholars, and that he used to treat the sick with medicines, and gave them the illusion that the benefit came to them only through his supplication. They say he healed a group of sick people on the Sabbath, and the Jews denounced him for this. He said to them: "Tell me about a sheep among the flock if it falls into a well: will you not go down to it and violate the Sabbath to rescue it?"

They said: "Yes." He said: "Then why do you violate the Sabbath to rescue a sheep, and not violate it to rescue a human being, who is of greater sanctity than a sheep?" And they were silenced.

They also relate about him that he walked with a group of his disciples on a mountain, and no food was brought to them, so he permitted them to take grass on the Sabbath. The Jews denounced him for cutting grass on the Sabbath. He said to them: "Tell me: if one of you were alone with a people of a different religion, and they ordered him to cut plants and throw them to their animals, not intending thereby to abolish the Sabbath, would you not permit him to cut plants?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then these people I ordered to cut plants so that they might eat and nourish themselves with it, not to break the Sabbath."

Among the wonders is that in the Torah in their hands is: "The kingship shall not depart from the house of Judah, nor the lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes." They cannot deny this. So it is said to them: You were people of dominion until the Messiah appeared, then your kingship ended, and today you have no kingdom. This is a proof that the Messiah has been sent.

From the time the Messiah was sent and they disbelieved in him and sought to kill him, the kings of Rome gained mastery over the Jews and Jerusalem, their dominion ended, and their unity was scattered.

They are asked: What do you say about ʿIsa ibn Maryam?

They say: He is the son of Joseph the carpenter, born of illegitimacy and not of legitimate marriage, and he had learned the greatest name of Allah and used it to work much sorcery.

Also among this wrathful people: that Allah the Exalted had revealed to Moses ʿalayhi al-salām the name composed of forty-two letters, and by it he split the sea and performed miracles.

It is said to them: If Moses performed miracles by the name of Allah, why did you affirm his prophethood and acknowledge it, yet deny the prophethood of ʿIsa, who performed miracles by the greatest name? Some of them answered this argument by saying that Allah the Exalted taught Moses that name, teaching him by revelation, whereas ʿIsa learned it from the walls of Jerusalem.

This is what befits their slander and their lying against Allah and His prophets. It closes against them the knowledge of Moses' prophethood, because both messengers shared in miracles and manifest signs that no one can match. If one of them learned them by trickery or by knowledge, then the other is equally possible in his case.

Both of them also reported that Allah the Exalted is the One who caused those things to occur by their hands, and that they were not of their own making. So rejecting one and affirming the other is dividing between things that are alike.

Furthermore, there is no proof for them that Moses received those miracles from Allah the Exalted except that it also indicates that ʿIsa ʿalayhi al-salām received them from Allah the Exalted as well. If it is possible to discredit the miracles of ʿIsa, it is possible to discredit the miracles of Moses ʿalayhi al-salām. And if that is false, this is also false.

If this is the state of the miracles of these two messengers, despite the distance of time, the scattering of their two communities across the earth, and the cessation of their miracles, then what is to be thought of the prophethood of one whose miracles and signs exceed a thousand? The time of them is near, their transmitters are the most truthful and most pious of creation, and their transmission is established by mass transmission (tawātur) generation after generation. The greatest of their miracles is a book that remains, fresh and new, unchanged, none of it altered or substituted, as though it were being sent down now: the Great Qur'an. And what it reports occurs at every time in the manner it described, as though one were witnessing it directly.

(Section)

The opinions of people have differed concerning the Torah in their hands: is it altered, or did the alteration and distortion occur only in interpretation and not in the revelation itself?

There are three positions: two extremes and a middle.

One group went to excess and claimed that all of it or most of it is altered and changed, and is not the Torah that Allah the Exalted revealed to Moses ʿalayhi al-salām. These people pointed out its contradictions and the contradiction of some parts with others.

Some of them went to an extreme and permitted cleaning oneself after urination with it.

Opposed to them was another group of imams of hadith, jurisprudence and theology, who said: rather, the alteration occurred in the interpretation, not in the revelation.

This is the position of Abu ʿAbdullah Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bukhari.

He said in his Sahih: "Yuḥarrifūn means yuzīlūn (they remove). No one removes a word from a book of Allah the Exalted, but they distort it: they interpret it other than its true interpretation."

This is the view chosen by al-Razi in his tafsir.

I heard our shaykh say: a dispute over this question arose among some excellent scholars. One of them chose this position and weakened the other, so he was denounced, and he brought them fifteen transmitted reports supporting it.

The argument of these people is that the Torah has spread to the eastern and western parts of the earth and has spread north and south, and no one knows the number of its copies except Allah the Exalted. It is impossible that all those copies were agreed upon to be altered and changed, such that no copy remains on earth that is not altered and changed, and the alteration follows a single method. This is something the intellect deems impossible and that testifies to its falsity.

They said: Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ, arguing against the Jews with it: ﴿Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 93]

They said: They agreed on abandoning the punishment of stoning, and they could not alter it from the Torah. For this reason, when they recited it to the Prophet ﷺ, the reader placed his hand on the verse of stoning. ʿAbdullah ibn Salam said to him:

"Lift your hand from the verse of stoning."

He lifted it, and beneath it the verse was shining. If they had altered the wording of the Torah, this would have been among the most important things they altered.

They said: Likewise, the description of the Prophet ﷺ and his emergence are in the Torah very clearly. They could not remove or change it. Allah censured them only for concealing it. Whenever he was argued against with what is in the Torah concerning his description and attributes, they would say: "It is not him, and we are awaiting him."

They said: Abu Dawud related in his Sunan from Ibn ʿUmar radiya Allahu ʿanhu, who said:

"A group of Jews came and invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to al-Qufff, so he came to them in the house of study (bayt al-midrās). They said: 'O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed fornication with a woman; judge between us.' They placed a cushion for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he sat on it, then said: 'Bring me the Torah.' It was brought, and he removed the cushion from beneath him and placed the Torah upon it, and said: 'I believe in You and in the One who sent You down.' Then he said: 'Bring me your most learned man.' A young man was brought..." and he mentioned the story of the stoning.

They said: If it had been altered and changed, he would not have placed it on the cushion, nor would he have said: "I believe in You and in the One who sent You down."

They said: Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; none can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-Anʿām: 115] And the Torah is among His words.

They said: The reports concerning the Jews' concealment of the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Torah, and their preventing their children and common folk from looking at it, are well known. And whoever among them looked at it, they told him: "It is not him."

This is some of what this group argued with.

A third group took a middle position and said: additions have been made to it, and some words have been changed, but most of it remains as it was revealed, and the alteration is very little in a small part of it.

Among those who chose this view is our shaykh in his book "al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man Baddala Din al-Masih."

He said: This is like what is in their Torah: that Allah the Exalted said to Abraham ʿalayhi al-salām: "Sacrifice your son, your firstborn, your only one, Isaac," an addition made by them to the wording of the Torah.

I say: This is clearly false for ten reasons.

The point is: this wording is among what they added to the Torah.

We will mention the reason that caused what was altered in it to be altered, for the truth is more deserving of being followed. So do not go to extremes like those who belittle it and mock it; rather, may Allah forbid such a thing. Nor do we say that it remains entirely as it was revealed, as the Qur'an does.

So we say, and with Allah is success:

The scholars and rabbis of the Jews believe that this Torah in their hands is not the very one that Allah the Exalted revealed to Moses son of ʿImran. This is because Moses ʿalayhi al-salām safeguarded the Torah from the Children of Israel, fearing that after him they would differ over its interpretation, which would lead to their division into factions. He entrusted it only to his kinsmen, the sons of Levi.

The proof of this is his saying in the Torah: "And Moses wrote this Torah and gave it to the Children of Israel, to the imams from the sons of Levi."

The sons of Aaron were the judges and rulers of the Jews, because leadership, service of the offerings and the House of the Holy were entrusted to them. Moses ʿalayhi al-salām gave the Children of Israel of the Torah only half a surah, and it is the one in which he said: "And Moses wrote this surah and taught it to the Children of Israel."

This is the text of the Torah in their hands; he said: "And let this surah be a witness for me against the Children of Israel."

And in it: Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, this surah shall not be forgotten from the mouths of their children."

This passage means that this surah contains a condemnation of their dispositions, and that they would oppose the laws of the Torah. Wrath would then come upon them, their dwellings would be ruined, and they would be taken captive into the lands. So this surah would be recited on their tongues, as a witness against them and as an establishment of the truth of what was said to them.

The Torah stated that this surah would not be forgotten from the mouths of their children. This shows that other surahs are not like this, and that it is possible for them to be forgotten from their mouths.

This indicates that Musa (peace be upon him) gave the Children of Israel from the Torah only this surah. As for the rest of it, he handed it to the sons of Harun, placed it with them, and protected it from others.

These Harunid leaders, who knew the Torah and memorised most of it, were killed by Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) in a single massacre on the day he conquered Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). Memorising the Torah was not obligatory upon them, nor was it a sunnah. Rather, each of the Harunids memorised a section of the Torah.

When Ezra (Ezra) saw that the people's temple had been burned, their dominion had ended, and their community had been scattered, and that their book had been lifted up, he gathered together what had been memorised, and from the sections that the priests had memorised came this Torah that is in their hands. For this reason they exaggerated greatly in glorifying Ezra.

They claim that a light now appears over his grave, and that it is in the marshes of Iraq, because he collected for them what would preserve their religion.

Some of them went to excess concerning him, to the point that one said: "He is the son of God." For this reason God, exalted is He, attributed this to the Jews as a people, to their race, and not to each individual among them.

So the Torah that is in their hands is in reality the book of Ezra, and in it is much of the Torah that God, exalted is He, sent down to Musa (peace be upon him). Then it passed through a nation that God has torn apart completely and scattered its unity, and three matters befell it:

The first: some addition and subtraction.

The second: differences of translation.

The third: differences of interpretation and exegesis.

We will mention examples of this to clarify the reality of the situation.

Example one:

The text quoted earlier: "And the flesh of prey in the field you shall not eat; you shall throw it to the dog."

The earlier explanation of their distortion of this text, and their taking it away from its intended meaning, has already been mentioned.

Example two:

Their statement in the Torah: "A prophet I will raise up for them from among their brothers, like you, to him they shall believe."

They distorted its interpretation, since they could not alter its revelation, and they said: "This is good news of a prophet from the Children of Israel." This is false for several reasons.

The first: if he had intended that, he would have said "from among themselves," as He said concerning Muhammad (peace be upon him): ﴿Allah certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾ [Al-i Imran: 164], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves﴾ [At-Tawbah: 128]. He did not say "from among your brothers."

The second: what is known in the Torah is that their brothers are other than the Children of Israel.

In the first part of the Fifth Book is His statement: "You are passing through the borders of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir. Beware that you covet nothing of their land."

So if the sons of Esau are brothers of the Children of Israel, since Esau and Israel were sons of Isaac, then the Romans are the sons of Esau, and the Jews are the sons of Israel, and they are their brothers. Likewise the sons of Ishmael are brothers of all the sons of Ibrahim.

The third: if this good news was about Samuel or someone else from the Children of Israel, it would not be correct to say "the Children of Israel are brothers of the Children of Israel." What is understood from this is that the sons of Ishmael or the sons of Esau are the brothers of the Children of Israel.

The fourth: He said: "I will raise up for them a prophet like you," and in another place: "He will be sent down the Torah like the Torah of Musa."

It is known that Samuel and other prophets of the Children of Israel were not like Musa, especially since the Torah says: "No one will arise among the Children of Israel like Musa."

Furthermore, among the Children of Israel, none received a Torah like the Torah of Musa except Muhammad and the Messiah (peace be upon them). The Messiah was from among the souls of the Children of Israel, not from their brothers, unlike Muhammad (peace be upon him), who was from their brothers, the sons of Ishmael.

Also, in some wordings of this text is: "To him you shall all listen." Samuel did not come with any addition or abrogation, because he was only sent to strengthen their hands against the people of Palestine, and to return them to the law of the Torah. He did not bring a new law or a new book. His ruling was that of all the other prophets from the Children of Israel, for the prophets used to govern them. Whenever one prophet died, another arose among them.

If this good news was for Samuel, then it is good news of all the prophets who were sent among them, and they would all be like Musa (peace be upon him), and a book like the book of Musa (peace be upon him) would have been sent down to each of them.

Example three:

Their statement in the Torah: "God, exalted is He, came from Mount Sinai, His light shone forth from Seir, and He manifested Himself from the mountains of Paran, and with Him were myriads of the holy ones."

They know that the mountain of Seir is the mountain of Sarat, which is inhabited by the sons of Esau, who believed in Isa (Jesus). They know that on this mountain was the station of the Messiah. They know that Sinai is the mountain of Tur.

As for the mountains of Paran, they interpret them as the mountains of Syria. This is from their slander and their distortion of interpretation.

The mountains of Paran are the mountains of Makkah, and "Paran" is one of the names of Makkah. The text of the Torah has indicated this: that when Ishmael separated from his father, he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, which is the mountains of Makkah. The wording of the Torah is: "Ishmael dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother married him to a woman from the land of Egypt."

So it is established by the text of the Torah that the mountains of Paran are a dwelling for the descendants of Ishmael. And if the Torah has pointed to a prophethood that would descend upon the mountains of Paran, it follows that it would descend upon the descendants of Ishmael, because they are its inhabitants.

It is known by necessity that it was not sent down upon anyone from the descendants of Ishmael (peace be upon him) other than Muhammad (peace be upon him).

This is among the most evident matters, praise be to God, exalted is He.

(Section)

Among what shows the coarseness of the understanding of this wrathful nation, the scarcity of their comprehension, the corruption of their opinions and their intellects, is what is in the Torah: "They are a people devoid of counsel; there is no understanding in them." They heard in the Torah: "The firstfruits of your land you shall bring to the house of the Lord your God, and you shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk."
