"He (ﷺ) would be in his house serving his family, and he never took revenge for himself."

He (ﷺ) "would mend his sandal, patch his garment, milk the goat for his family, feed the camel, and eat with the servant. He would sit with the poor, walk with the widow and the orphan in their needs, begin with peace whoever he met, and answer the invitation of whoever invited him, even to the least thing."

"He (ﷺ) was easy in his dealings, gentle in character, noble in disposition, good in companionship, open-faced and smiling, humble without abasement, generous without extravagance, tender-hearted and merciful to every Muslim, lowering his wing to the believers, gentle towards them."

He (ﷺ) also said: "Shall I inform you of whom the Fire is forbidden, or who is forbidden the Fire? It is forbidden for every near, easy, gentle, soft person." Related by al-Tirmidhi, who said: a good hadith.

He said: "If I were invited to a foreleg, or a shank, I would accept; and if a foreleg, or a shank, were given to me as a gift, I would accept." Related by al-Bukhari.

He (ﷺ) "would visit the sick, attend funerals, ride a donkey, and answer the invitation of a slave."

"On the day of Qurayzah he was on a donkey bridled with a rope of palm fibre, with a saddle of palm fibre beneath him."

[Section: Kinds of love]

Here there are four kinds of love which must be distinguished, and it is only through failing to distinguish between them that whoever went astray did so.

The first: love of God. It alone does not suffice for salvation from the punishment of God or for success in His reward, for the polytheists, the worshippers of the cross, the Jews, and others also love God.

The second: love of what God loves. This is what brings a person into Islam and removes him from disbelief, and the people most beloved to God are those who are most upright in this love and most intense in it.

The third: love for God and for His sake, which is a requirement of loving what He loves. The love of what He loves is not sound except for His sake and through Him.

The fourth: love alongside God, which is idolatrous love. Whoever loves something alongside God, not for God, nor for His sake, nor in Him, has taken it as a rival besides God, and this is the love of the polytheists.

There remains a fifth kind, which is not part of what we are discussing: natural love, which is a human's inclination towards what suits his nature, such as the thirsty person's love for water, the hungry person's love for food, and love of sleep, of a wife, and of a child. Such love is not blamed except when it diverts from the remembrance of God and occupies one from His love, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Men whom neither commerce nor sale diverts from the remembrance of God﴾ [al-Nur: 37].

Indeed, part of complete trust in God (tawakkul) is adopting the means (asbab) that God has established as causes for their effects, both by divine decree and by divine law. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions were the most complete in trust in God, and they met their enemies while protecting themselves with various kinds of weapons. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered Mecca with a helmet on his head, and God had already revealed to him: ﴿And God will protect you from the people﴾.

Many people who lack verification and firm grounding in knowledge find this problematic, and they try to be clever in answering it. Sometimes they say that he did this to teach the community, and sometimes that this happened before the verse was revealed. A question arose in Egypt that one of the rulers asked about. He was told a hadith that Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir mentioned in his large History (Tarikhihi al-Kabir): that after the Jewish woman sent him a poisoned sheep, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would not eat any food that was brought to him until the one who brought it had eaten from it first.

They said: In this there is an example for kings in this matter.

Someone said: How can this be reconciled with God's words, Exalted is He: ﴿And God will protect you from the people﴾? If God, glorified is He, has guaranteed him protection, then He knows that no human has a way to reach him.

Some answered that this indicates the hadith is weak, and others that this happened before the verse was revealed, so that after it was revealed he would not have done that. If these people had reflected that God's guarantee of protection for him does not contradict his taking the means to it, it would have spared them this strained effort. This guarantee from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, does not contradict his guarding himself against people, nor does it negate it. Just as God's telling him that He will make His religion prevail over all religions and exalt it does not contradict His command to him to fight, to prepare equipment, strength, and horses for battle, to take caution, vigilance and precaution against his enemy, and to fight them with various kinds of war and tawriya (misdirection). So when he wanted to launch a campaign, he would make it appear to be heading elsewhere. This is because that statement from God, glorified is He, is information about the outcome and destiny of his condition, through the means he pursued, which God made lead to that and necessitate it. He (ﷺ) knew best about his Lord and was most devoted to His command, so he would never neglect the means that God, in His wisdom, made necessary for what He promised him: the victory and triumph of making His religion manifest and overcoming his enemy. This is like how God guaranteed him life until he conveyed his messages and made his religion manifest, while he still pursued the means of life, such as food, drink, clothing and shelter. This is a point where many people err, to the extent that some of them abandoned supplication (du'a'), claiming there was no benefit in it, because: if what is asked for has been decreed, it will be attained without fail, and if it has not been decreed, it will not be attained. So what benefit is there in occupying oneself with supplication?

Then he tried to be clever in his answer, saying: Supplication is an act of worship. It is said to this person who errs: there remains another part, which is the truth, that God has decreed for him his desired goal through a cause such that if he pursues it, the goal is achieved for him, and if he neglects the cause, the goal is lost to him. Supplication is among the greatest causes for obtaining what is desired. The example of this person who errs is only like one who says: If God has decreed that I be satisfied, I will be satisfied whether I eat or not; if He has not decreed satisfaction for me, I will not be satisfied whether I eat or not. So what is the benefit of eating? These are false trifles that contradict the wisdom of God, the Exalted, and His law. And success is from God.

(Benefit)

Utba ibn Abi Waqqas, who broke the Prophet's (ﷺ) incisor at the Battle of Uhud, some scholars of reports said, after tracing his descendants, that none of them reached puberty without having bad breath and a deformity of the teeth or mouth, which is recognized among them as a consequence of the fathers' misdeeds falling on the sons.

Scholars differed about what happened to the Prophet (ﷺ) of this kind and similar. It was said that it occurred before the revelation of His words: ﴿And God will protect you from the people﴾.

It was also said that the protection promised was protection of the self from being killed, not complete protection from their harm. God left his Messenger with the reward of that harm, and gave his community the good example of following him: when any of them is harmed, he looks at what he endured and is patient. And for the wicked harmers, there is a seizing that will grow (al-akhdhah al-rabiyah).

This is an address to the Christians, because it comes in the context of His address to them with His words: ﴿Certainly those who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary," have disbelieved. And the Messiah had said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ up to His words: ﴿and they had strayed from the sound way.﴾ He described them as having strayed first, and then as having led many astray, who were their followers.

This was before the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), when they went astray regarding the matter of the Messiah and led their followers astray. Then, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, they increased in another kind of straying by denying him and disbelieving in him, so their straying was multiplied. This is the view of a group of them, including al-Zamakhshari (d. 538 AH) and others, but it is weak. All of this is a description of their predecessors, whom these people follow. He described them with three attributes: first, that they had strayed before; second, that they led their followers astray; third, that they strayed from the sound way. These are attributes of their predecessors, whose desires these (present people) were forbidden to follow. Therefore it is not valid that it describes those who existed in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), because they are the ones being addressed by the prohibition, not those prohibited. So reflect on this.

The secret of the verse is that it necessitates the repetition of straying in the Christians, straying after straying, because of the extreme of their ignorance of the truth. It is similar to the verse mentioned earlier concerning the repetition of anger against the Jews. For this reason the Christians are more specifically associated with straying than the Jews. The reason for the repetition of this straying is that straying misses its very aim, so the one who strays is misguided in it. He intends what he should not intend and worships what he should not worship. He may also hit a true aim but stray on the path and means that lead to it. The first is straying in the end, and the second is straying in the means. Then, if he calls others to that, he has led them astray. The predecessors of the Christians combined all three types: they strayed from their aim, since they did not reach it, and they claimed that their god was a human who eats, drinks, weeps, and was killed, crucified, and slapped. This is straying in the very aim, since they did not attain it, and they strayed from the path leading to it. Thus they were not guided to the sought-after goal nor to the way leading to it. They called their followers to this, so they strayed from the truth and from its path and led many astray. Therefore they were more deeply in error than the Jews, and they were described with the more specific of the two attributes.

What confirms this is that the Jews came from corruption of will, envy, and preferring what they had of worldly gain and leadership over their people, so they feared that Islam would take it away. They were not afflicted through lack of knowledge of the truth, for they knew that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as they know their own sons. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, did not rebuke and reproach them except for their corrupt wills: arrogance, envy, preferring unlawful gain, transgression, and killing the Prophets. He rebuked the Christians for straying and ignorance, which is the lack of knowledge of the truth. Misery and disbelief arise sometimes from failing to recognize the truth and sometimes from failing to will it and act upon it, and they may combine. The disbelief of the Jews arose from not willing the truth and acting upon it, and from preferring something else over it after recognizing it, so it was not pure straying. The disbelief of the Christians arose from their ignorance of the truth and their straying regarding it. So when it becomes clear to them and they prefer falsehood over it, they resemble the people of anger and remain "those who have earned anger and who have gone astray." Then, since guidance, success, and happiness cannot be attained except by knowing the truth and preferring it over other things, and since ignorance prevents the servant from knowing the truth and transgression prevents him from willing it, the servant is most in need of asking Allah, the Exalted, at all times to guide him to the straight path, by teaching, explaining, guiding, inspiring, granting success, and helping him, so that He teaches him and makes him know, then makes him one who wills it and intends to follow it. Thus he exits the way of those who have earned anger, who turned away from it knowingly and deliberately, and of those who have gone astray, who turned away from it through ignorance and error.

(Benefit)

The predecessors used to say: whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians.

This is as they said. Whoever among the scholars becomes corrupt and adopts the characteristics of the Jews, such as distorting words from their places, concealing what Allah has sent down when it threatens his aim, envying those whom Allah has given of His bounty, seeking to kill, and killing people who enjoin justice and call them to the Book of their Lord and the Sunnah of their Prophet, and other characteristics for which the Jews were blamed, such as disbelief, distortion, concealment, altering, cunning to get around what is forbidden, and mixing truth with falsehood, then his resemblance to the Jews is clear.

As for whoever among the worshippers becomes corrupt, worshipping Allah according to his own desire and not by what His Messenger (ﷺ) was sent with, and exaggerating regarding the shaykhs by placing them in the station of lordship, and going beyond that into some form of incarnation or unification, then his resemblance to the Christians is clear.

So the Muslim must keep as far away as possible from these two resemblances. Whoever contemplates these two resemblances and attributes and knows the conditions of people will know his necessity and need for this supplication, which is the most beneficial supplication a servant has and the most obligatory upon him. His need for it is greater than his need for life and self, because the most that is lost by losing those two is death, whereas by losing this he suffers eternal misery. So we ask Allah to guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who have earned anger nor of those who have gone astray. Amen. Indeed He is near and responsive.

(Section)

Allah has forbidden exaggeration (ghuluw) in His words: ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess (taghlu) in your religion beyond the truth.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 77].

Exaggeration is of two kinds. One kind takes a person out of being obedient, such as one who adds a unit of prayer, or fasts perpetually including the days on which fasting is forbidden, or throws the pebbles at the Jamarat with large stones like those thrown from a catapult (manjaniq), or runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah ten times, or the like, intentionally.

The other kind is exaggeration that causes fear of discontinuation and exhaustion, such as standing in prayer the whole night, or continuous fasting all the time without fasting the days on which fasting is forbidden, and oppressing oneself in acts of worship and litanies. Concerning this the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed this religion is ease, and no one makes the religion difficult except that it overcomes him. So be steadfast, approach (the goal), and give good news, and seek help by (worshipping in) the morning, the afternoon, and a portion of the night." He meant: seek help in obeying Allah by acts performed in these three times, for the traveler seeks help in covering the distance of the journey by traveling during them.

The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "Let one of you pray with his energy; when he becomes weary, let him sleep." Both are narrated by al-Bukhari.

In Sahih Muslim, from him (ﷺ), that he said, three times: "The extremists (al-mutanatti'un) are destroyed," and they are those who go to excess (al-mutaʿammiqun) and those who are harsh upon themselves (al-mutashaddidun).

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from him (ﷺ): "Take upon yourselves only the deeds you can sustain, for by Allah, Allah does not tire until you tire."

In the Sunan, from him (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed this religion is firm, so proceed in it gently, and do not make the worship of Allah hateful to yourself," or as he said.

His words: "and not to be carried upon a cause that weakens submission."

He means: that one should not interpret a command or prohibition with a cause that would nullify them, as some interpreted the prohibition of wine as being caused by the arousing of enmity and hatred and exposure to corruption. So if one is safe from this danger, drinking it becomes permissible, as it has been said:

Pour it, for its prohibition is not for its own sake,
but because of causes that intoxication contains.

If there is no intoxication that leads away from guidance,
then water in the glass and wine are equal.

This has reached some peoples to the point of complete departure from religion. Some scholars have carried this to the extent of making the prohibition of other than grape wine caused by intoxication, so one may drink whatever he wishes, as long as it does not intoxicate.

Among the causes that weaken submission is that one gives a ruling a weak cause which was not in reality what motivated it. Then the servant's submission weakens when he believes this is the cause of the ruling. For this reason the way of the people (the early generations) was not to delve into the reasons for obligations, out of fear of this danger.

In some ancient reports: "O Children of Israel, do not say: Why did our Lord command? But say: With what did our Lord command?"

Also, if one does not comply with a command until its cause becomes clear to him, he is not submitting to the command. The least of its degrees is that his submission to it weakens.

Also, if he looks at the wisdoms of acts of worship and obligations, for example, and makes their cause the gathering of the heart and turning it toward Allah, and says: "I occupy myself with the aim rather than the means," then he occupies himself with his own inner gathering and solitude, and leaves off the litanies of the forms of worship, thus suspending them, and abandons submission by taking the command to be based on a cause that removed his submission.

All of this comes from abandoning the magnification of commands and prohibitions.

Into many groups has entered from this corruption what none knows except Allah. None knows how far corrupt causes have weakened submission except Allah. How much has it nullified of Allah's commands, permitted of prohibitions, and made unlawful of what is permitted?!

This is what the predecessors unanimously agreed in condemning.

[The Reality of Knowledge (ma'rifa)]

The author of al-Manazil said: "Chapter on Gnosis (ma'rifa)." God Most High said: ﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 83]. Ma'rifa (gnosis, recognition): the encompassing of a thing's reality as it is.

I say: The Qur'an contains both the term ma'rifa and the term 'ilm (knowledge). The term ma'rifa appears in His saying: ﴿because of the truth they have recognized﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 83], and His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqara: 146].

As for the term 'ilm, it is broader in application, as in His saying: ﴿So know that there is no god but Allah﴾ [Muhammad: 19]; His saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18], to the end of the verse; His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth﴾ [al-An'am: 114]; His saying: ﴿And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 114]; His saying: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19]; His saying: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]; His saying: ﴿But those who have been given knowledge and faith will say: You have remained, by the decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Rum: 56]; His saying: ﴿But those who had been given knowledge said: Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteous deeds﴾ [al-Qasas: 80]; His saying: ﴿And these examples We present to the people, but none understands them except the knowing﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 43]; His saying: ﴿One who had knowledge of the Book said﴾ [al-Naml: 40]; His saying: ﴿Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death﴾ [al-Hadid: 17]; His saying: ﴿Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement﴾ [al-Hadid: 20]; His saying: ﴿And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him﴾ [al-Baqara: 223]; His saying: ﴿So know that it was sent down with the knowledge of Allah﴾ [Hud: 14]. And this is abundant.

Allah, glorified is He, chose for Himself the name "Knowledge" and its derivatives: He described Himself as ʿAlim (Knowing), ʿAlim (All-Knowing), ʿAllam (Exceedingly Knowing), ʿalima (He knew), and yaʿlamu (He knows), and He informed that He has knowledge, rather than using the term ma'rifa in the Qur'an. It is known that the name Allah chose for Himself is the most perfect of its kind, sharing its meaning with Him.

The term ma'rifa came in the Qur'an specifically regarding the believers among the People of the Book, as in His saying: ﴿That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 82], up to His saying ﴿because of the truth they have recognized﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 83], and His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqara: 146].

This group greatly prefers ma'rifa over 'ilm. Many of them do not elevate 'ilm at all, and regard it as a barrier and a veil preventing ma'rifa. Among the people of steadfastness (istiqama) of this group, they are the most emphatic in urging the seekers (murids) to acquire knowledge, and they hold that no one can be a complete friend (wali) of Allah without the people of knowledge, ever. Allah has not taken, and does not take, an ignorant friend, and ignorance is the root of every innovation, misguidance and deficiency, while knowledge is the root of all good, guidance and perfection.

**Some of the errors into which the people of words and the people of meanings fell**

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who believe! Intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous altars, and divining arrows are only an abomination of Satan's work. So avoid it that you may be successful.﴾ The word *khamr* (intoxicant) is general and covers every intoxicating drink. Excluding some intoxicating drinks from the scope of the term *khamr* is to curtail it and diminish its generality. Rather, the truth is what the Lawgiver said: "Every intoxicant is *khamr*." Likewise, excluding some kinds of *maysir* (gambling) from the scope of its term is also to curtail it and diminish its meaning. What, then, made backgammon (*nard*), which involves no stake, a form of *maysir* while excluding chess (*shatranj*), even though it is among the clearest forms of *maysir*, as more than one of the early scholars (*salaf*) said: "It is *maysir*"? And 'Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, said: "It is the *maysir* of the non-Arabs (*'ajam*)."

**(Benefit)**

The performance of what is commanded is sought for its own sake, while the abandonment of what is forbidden is sought for the completion of the performance of what is commanded. Thus, a prohibited act is forbidden because it disrupts the performance of the command or weakens and diminishes it, as Allah, glorified is He, pointed out regarding the prohibition of intoxicants and gambling, by their barring people from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. Prohibited acts are therefore obstacles and impediments that prevent the performance of commanded acts or their perfection. Thus, the prohibition of them is for the sake of something else, while the command to perform obligatory acts is for their own sake.

He also said:

The performance of what is commanded is sought for its own sake, so it is legislated as a purpose of the Law. The knowledge of Allah, His Oneness, His worship alone, turning to Him in repentance, relying on Him, sincerity of deed toward Him, loving Him, being content with Him, and standing in His service is the end for which creation was made and by which the command was established. This is a matter sought for its own sake. The forbidden acts were prohibited only because they bar from that, or distract from it, or cause its perfection to be lost. For this reason, the degrees of their prohibition correspond to the extent to which they bar one from the commanded act, hinder one from it, or cause its perfection to be lost. Thus, the forbidden is sought for the sake of something else, while the commanded is sought for its own sake. Had intoxicants and gambling not barred one from the remembrance of Allah, from the prayer, and from the mutual affection and love that Allah placed among His servants, He would not have prohibited them. Likewise, had they not come between the servant and his intellect, by which he knows Allah, worships Him, praises Him, glorifies Him, prays to Him, and prostrates to Him, He would not have prohibited them. So too with the rest of what He has prohibited: He prohibited it only because it bars one from what He loves and is pleased with, and comes between the servant and its perfection.

**[Section: The wisdom in prescribing the *hadd* (fixed penalty) for drinking a single drop of intoxicant]**

As for his statement: "He prescribed the *hadd* for a single drop of intoxicant but not for many liters of urine," this too is part of the perfection of the Law, its conformity with reason and natural disposition, and its upholding of benefits. Allah, glorified is He, placed in the natural constitution of creatures an aversion to such things and a repulsion from them, and so He dispensed with a deterrent by way of *hadd* for them, because the natural restraint is sufficient to prevent them.

As for what the natural inclinations strongly crave, He intensified the punishment for it in proportion to the strength of the natural craving for it. He also blocked the means leading to it, whether near or far (*sadd al-dhara'i'*, blocking the means), and made what surrounds it a protected zone (*hima*), and forbade approaching it. For this reason, He punished adultery with the most heinous forms of killing, theft with the cutting off of the hand, and drinking intoxicants with the lashing of the whip. He also forbade a small quantity of intoxicant even if it does not intoxicate, since a small amount calls to a large amount. For this reason, whoever permitted from intoxicating date-wine (*nabidh*) the amount that does not intoxicate went beyond pure analogy, wisdom, and the requirement of the texts.

Moreover, the corruption and harm in drinking intoxicants, both the harm confined to the drinker and the harm extending to others, are many times greater than the corruption and harm in drinking urine and eating filth, for the harm of the latter is confined to the one who consumes it.

**(Benefit)**

Allah, exalted is He, prohibited intoxicants because of the many corruptions that follow from the loss of the intellect. This is not what we are concerned with here. Rather, He prohibited even a single drop of it, and prohibited keeping it for making vinegar (*takhlil*) and its impurity, lest a drop become a pretext for a sip, and keeping it for vinegar become a pretext for keeping it for drinking. Then He went to great lengths in blocking the means, so He forbade mixing two kinds of drink (*khalitayn*), drinking fresh juice after three days, and fermenting drinks in vessels in which wine may ferment without one's knowing. This was to cut off the root of approaching intoxicants. The Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stated the reason for the prohibition of even a small amount when he said: "If I were to permit you this, you would soon make it like this," [meaning the intoxicant].

**(Benefit)**

Those who deny meanings and wisdom in the Law objected to those who affirm them, saying: "The Law has differentiated between like things: it prescribed the *hadd* for drinking intoxicants but did not prescribe it for drinking blood, urine, and eating excrement, though these are more foul than intoxicants. It prescribed cutting off the hand for stealing a quarter dinar, but did not prescribe cutting it off for plundering a thousand dinars. It prescribed the *hadd* for accusing a man of fornication but did not prescribe it for accusing him of unbelief (*kufr*), though the latter is greater. It did not stipulate a *hadd* for usury (*riba*) though it is among the major sins, while it stipulated the *hadd* for drinking intoxicants and fornication, which are also major sins."

The affirmers answered: "This indicates the consideration of meanings and wisdom, and the establishment of the Law according to the benefits of the servants. The Lawgiver looks at the corruption of the prohibited act, then looks at what restrains people from it and what drives them to it. When its corruption is great, he prescribes punishment in proportion to that corruption. If the natural dispositions that Allah, exalted is He, placed in the children of Adam serve as a restraint against it, He is content with that restraint and dispenses with the *hadd*. Thus, no *hadd* is prescribed for drinking urine, blood, vomit, or eating excrement, because people's natures shun these things, so they are not committed frequently enough to require deterrence by the *hadd*. This is unlike drinking intoxicants, fornication, and theft, where the motive for them is strong. Were the *hadd*s not prescribed for them, their corruptions would spread and the calamity of committing them would be great. As for plunder (*nahb*), no *hadd* is prescribed for it, either because the natural motives do not generally drive people to it, given the fear of disgrace, notoriety, and quick apprehension, or because its corruption is averted by relieving the people (from the plunderer) and by preventing the plunderer and seizing his hand."

"As for usury, no *hadd* is prescribed for it. It is said that this is because it takes place in markets and in public, so its removal was entrusted to the public's disapproval. This is unlike theft, fornication, and drinking intoxicants, which generally occur secretly. Had its removal been entrusted to people, it would not have been eliminated."

"A better explanation than this is that since the creditor (*murabi*) is only entitled to the return of his principal, if he takes the excess, he is judged to return it to the debtor, and if he does not take it, nothing more is awarded to him. Thus the corruption of usury is removed by this. If the debtor asked him, he would not give him anything but his principal. Therefore, when he agrees to give the excess, he has agreed to waste it and give it away for free, and the one who takes it has agreed to eat fire."

"Better than these two is to say: the sin of usury is too great to be purified by the *hadd*. The usurer is one who wars against Allah and His Messenger and eats fire. The *hadd* is prescribed only as purification and expiation. The sin of usury is not removed from him by the *hadd*, because its prohibition is greater than that. It is like the prohibition on one who deliberately breaks the fast of Ramadan without excuse, the one who withholds *zakat* out of stinginess, one who deliberately abandons the afternoon prayer, and one who deliberately abandons Friday prayer. For the *hadd*s are expiations and purifications, so they apply only to a sin that accepts expiation and purification. From this is the absence of a *hadd* for consuming the wealth of orphans, because the one who consumes it has already been deserving of the Fire, and the *hadd* does not avail in removing what is due to him of the Fire. Likewise, abandoning prayer is too great a matter to have a *hadd* prescribed for it. Similarly, the perjurious oath (*yamin al-ghamus*) is too great a sin to have a *hadd* or an expiation prescribed for it."

"When you reflect on the secrets of this perfect Law, you will find it in the utmost wisdom and attention to benefits. It never differentiates between like things, nor equates unlike things. It does not prohibit something for a corruption and then permit what has a corruption equal to or greater than what it prohibited. It does not permit something for a benefit and then prohibit what has a benefit equal to what it permitted. None of this is found at all in what the Messenger brought. Nor does it entail the statements based on people's opinions, assumptions, and personal reasonings."

"In those [legal positions opposed by these objectors] are found the differentiation between like things, the joining of unlike things, the permitting of a thing while prohibiting its look, and similar matters."

[Section: Financial penalties and their basis]

As for imposing financial penalty (taghrim al-mal), which is a monetary punishment, the Lawgiver prescribed it in several cases. Among them: burning the goods of one who embezzles from the spoils of war (ghanima); depriving him of his share; doubling the penalty upon the thief of fruit still hanging on the tree; doubling it upon one who conceals a lost item that was picked up; taking half the property of one who withholds zakat; and his ﷺ intention to burn the houses of those who do not pray in congregation, had it not been for what prevented him from carrying it out, namely that children and women are in them, so the punishment would extend to someone other than the offender, and that is not permissible, just as it is not permissible to punish a pregnant woman. Among them also is the punishment of one who behaves badly toward the commander in a military campaign by withholding the spoils of a slain enemy from the one who killed him, when this offender interceded on behalf of another and the commander ordered that it be given to the intercessor, so the one for whom intercession was made was deprived as a punishment to the one who interceded and ordered it.

[Financial penalty is of two kinds: fixed and unfixed]

This category of punishments has two kinds: a fixed kind and an unfixed kind. The fixed kind is what corresponds to the thing destroyed, either as a right of God, glory be to Him, such as the destruction of game during the state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state of pilgrimage), or as a right of a human being, such as the destruction of his property. God, glory be to Him, has drawn attention to the fact that the compensation for game involves a punishment, in His saying: ﴿that he may taste the evil consequence of his deed﴾.

Among this kind is requiting the offender with the opposite of what he intended, through deprivation, such as the punishment of one who kills his testator by depriving him of inheritance, the punishment of a mudabbar slave (a slave whose freedom is conditioned upon his master's death) who kills his master by the nullification of his tadbir (the arrangement for his freedom), and the punishment of a legatee by the nullification of his bequest. Of this category is also the punishment of a disobedient wife by the forfeiture of her maintenance and clothing.

As for the second kind, the unfixed one, this is what falls within the ijtihad (independent reasoning) of the imams according to the considerations of public benefit (maslahah). For this reason the Lawgiver did not bring a general command concerning it, nor a fixed measure that may not be increased or decreased, as with the hudud (fixed penalties). Therefore the jurists differed regarding it: is its ruling abrogated (mansukh) or established?

The correct view is that it varies with the variation of public benefit, and it is referred to the ijtihad of the imams in every time and place according to what is beneficial; since there is no evidence of abrogation, and the rightly-guided caliphs and those after them among the imams have acted upon it.

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father), in his explanation of this verse, said: "If all the people were to abandon the Hajj, the sky would fall upon the earth."

He also said: "If all the people were to abandon the Hajj, they would not be given respite."

The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that at the end of time Allah will lift His House from the earth, and His speech from the mushafs and from the breasts of men, so that no House will remain on earth to be visited for Hajj, and no speech will remain to be recited. At that point the destruction of the world will be near.

Likewise, the state of people today: their standing is by the standing of the traces of their Prophet and his laws among them, and the establishment of their affairs is by the attainment of their interests and the repelling from them of all kinds of calamity and evil, according to the degree to which those traces appear and stand among them. Their ruin, their distress, and the descent of calamity and evil upon them occur when those laws are neglected, turned away from, when judgment is sought from other than them, and when something else is taken in their place.

Whoever reflects on how Allah, glory be to Him, gives power over the lands and the servants to the enemies He empowers will know that this is due to their neglect of the religion of their Prophet, his sunnah and his laws. So Allah empowers over them those who destroy them and take vengeance upon them, to the extent that the lands in which the traces, sunnah and laws of the Messenger (ﷺ) appear are protected from them in proportion to the appearance of that among them.

[Section: On what God has chosen among deeds and other things]

The point is that God, glory be to Him and exalted, chose from every kind of created thing its best, and reserved it for Himself and was pleased with it above all else. For He, exalted is He, is Good (ṭayyib) and loves only the good, and accepts from deed, speech and charity only what is good. Thus the good of everything is what He chooses.

As for His creation, it is general to both categories, and by this the sign of a servant's happiness and wretchedness is known. For the good suits only the good, is pleased only with it, is at rest only with it, and his heart is at peace only with it. Thus from speech he takes the good word (al-kalim al-ṭayyib), which rises to God, exalted is He, only by it, and he is most averse to indecency in speech, to foul language, abuse, lying, backbiting, slander, calumny, false speech, and every corrupt utterance.

Likewise, he cherishes from deeds only the best of them, which are the deeds on which sound natural disposition (fiṭar salīmah) together with the prophetic laws agree on their goodness, and which sound reason has approved. Thus the law, reason and natural disposition all agree on their goodness, such as worshipping God alone without associating anything with Him; preferring His good pleasure over his own desire; drawing near to Him with all his effort and capacity; doing good to His creatures as far as he can, treating them as he would like to be treated and as he would like them to treat him; leaving them alone in what he would like them to leave him alone; advising them as he advises himself; judging for them as he would like to be judged; bearing their harm and not making them bear his harm; refraining from their honor and not retaliating against them with what they have done to his honor; spreading the good he sees in them and concealing the evil he sees in them; and making excuses for them as far as he can in matters that do not nullify the law or contradict any command or prohibition of God.

He also has from character traits the best and purest of them, such as forbearance (ḥilm), dignity (waqār), tranquility (sakīnah), mercy (raḥmah), patience (ṣabr), faithfulness (wafā'), ease of disposition, gentleness of temper (līn al-ʿarīkah), truthfulness, a heart free from rancor (ghill), deceit (ghishsh), spite (ḥiqd) and envy (ḥasad), humility and lowering the wing to the people of faith, might and sternness toward the enemies of God, guarding his face from humiliating it and abasing it before other than God, chastity, courage, generosity, and manliness (murū'ah), and every trait on whose goodness the laws, natural dispositions and reason agree.

Likewise, he chooses from foods only the best of them, which is what is lawful, wholesome and pleasant, nourishing body and soul in the best manner, along with the servant's freedom from its consequence.

Likewise, he chooses from marriages only the best and purest of them, and from fragrance only the best and purest of it, and from companions and associates only the good among them. So his spirit is good, his body is good, his character is good, his deed is good, his speech is good, his food is good, his drink is good, his clothing is good, his marriage is good, his entering is good, his exiting is good, his returning is good, and his abode is all good.

This is among those of whom God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, "Peace be upon you; enter the Garden for what you used to do."﴾ [al-Naḥl: 32]

And among those to whom the keepers of the Garden will say: ﴿Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it, abiding forever.﴾ [al-Zumar: 73] This "fa'" (then) implies causation, i.e., because of your goodness, enter it.

And God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Bad women are for bad men, and bad men are for bad women; and good women are for good men, and good men are for good women.﴾ [al-Nūr: 26] The verse has been interpreted as meaning that bad words are for bad people and good words are for good people, and it has been interpreted as meaning that good women are for good men and bad women are for bad men, and it encompasses that and other things. So good words, deeds and women are for their suitable counterparts among the good, and bad words, deeds and women are for their suitable counterparts among the bad.

God, glory be to Him and exalted, made all the good in the Garden, and made all the bad in the Fire. He made the abodes three: an abode purified for the good, forbidden to other than the good, which gathers every good, and it is the Garden; and an abode purified for the bad and its evils, which none enter but the bad, and it is the Fire.

And an abode in which the good and the bad are mixed and blended together, and it is this abode. For this reason trial and affliction occur through this mixing and blending, in accordance with divine wisdom. When the Day of the Return of creation comes, God distinguishes the bad from the good: He places the good and its people in an abode apart, which others do not mix with, and places the bad and its people in an abode apart, which others do not mix with. Thus the matter returns to only two abodes: the Garden, which is the abode of the good, and the Fire, which is the abode of the bad. God brings into being, from the deeds of both groups, their reward and their punishment. He makes the good words, deeds and characters of the first group the very substance of their bliss and pleasures, and brings forth for them from these the most perfect causes of delight and joy. He makes the bad words, deeds and characters of the others the very substance of their torment and pains, and brings forth for them from these the greatest causes of punishment and pain, with consummate wisdom and overwhelming, dominating might, so that He may show His servants the perfection of His lordship, the perfection of His wisdom, knowledge, justice and mercy, and so that His enemies may know that they were the fabricators and liars, not His noble and truthful messengers. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that God will not resurrect whoever dies. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, but most of the people do not know. [He will do so] to make clear to them that about which they differ, and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.﴾ [al-Naḥl: 38-39]

The point is that God, glory be to Him and exalted, made for happiness and wretchedness signs by which they are known. The happy, good person is fit only for what is good, comes only with what is good, issues only what is good, and is associated only with what is good. The wretched, bad person is fit only for what is bad, comes only with what is bad, issues only what is bad, and from his heart the badness gushes out upon his tongue and limbs, while the good person's goodness gushes from his heart upon his tongue and limbs. A person may have two substances in him, and whichever of them predominates over him, he is of its people. If God wills good for him, He purifies him from the bad substance before the meeting, so he meets Him on the Day of Resurrection purified, and does not need to be purified by the Fire; He purifies him from it through what He enables him of sincere repentance, effacing good deeds, and expiating calamities, until he meets God with no sin upon him. And He withholds from the other the materials of purification, so he meets Him on the Day of Resurrection with a bad substance and a good substance. His wisdom, exalted is He, refuses that anyone with his evils should dwell in His abode, so He causes him to enter the Fire as purification, cleansing and refining for him. When the ingot of his faith is freed from impurity, he is then fit to dwell near Him and to live alongside the good among His servants.

The keeping of this type of people in the Fire is in proportion to the speed or slowness with which those evils leave them. The quickest of them to be rid of evil and purified are the quickest to leave, and the slowest are the slowest to leave: ﴿a recompense in accordance [with their deeds]﴾ [al-Naba': 26] ﴿and your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 46].

Since the polytheist is of corrupt origin and corrupt essence, the Fire does not purify his corruption; rather, even if he were to leave it, he would return corrupt as he was, like a dog that enters the sea and then comes out of it. For this reason God, exalted is He, forbade the Garden to the polytheist.

Since the believer who is good and makes others good is free from evils, the Fire is forbidden to him, as there is nothing in him that requires his purification by it. So glory be to Him whose wisdom dazzles minds and intellects, and whose creatures' natural dispositions and reason bear witness that He is the Wisest of judges and Lord of the worlds; there is no god but Him.

Abu 'Umar said: In the narration of Ashhab, Malik was asked about the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "I forbid you from qila wa qala (idle talk) and excessive questioning." He said: "As for excessive questioning, I do not know whether it is what you are engaged in, which he forbade you from, namely excessive questions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked questions and found fault with them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you﴾. I do not know whether this is what is meant, or whether it is asking people for charity in begging."

Al-Awza'i said, from 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah: "I wish that my share from the people of this time were that I neither ask them about anything nor they ask me. They multiply questions just as the people of dirhams multiply dirhams."

He said: They also argued with what Ibn Shihab narrated from 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he heard his father say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The greatest of the Muslims in crime against the Muslims is the one who asks about a thing which was not forbidden to the Muslims, and so it became forbidden for them because of his question."

Ibn Wahb also narrated, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. So when I forbid you from something, avoid it, and when I command you to something, take from it as much as you are able."

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said, from 'Amr, from Tawus, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said while on the pulpit: "I adjure by Allah every man who asks about a thing that has not happened, for Allah has already made clear what is to happen."

Abu 'Umar said: Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid and Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I have not seen a people better than the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They asked him only about thirteen questions until he passed away ﷺ, all of which are in the Qur'an: ﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222], ﴿They ask you about the sacred month﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217], ﴿They ask you about orphans﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220]. They asked him only about what would benefit them." Abu 'Umar said: The matter is not of the thirteen questions except three.

I say: Ibn 'Abbas's intention in his words "they asked him only about thirteen questions" is the questions which Allah related from them in the Qur'an. Otherwise, the questions they asked him and whose rulings he explained to them by the Sunnah are almost countless. However, they used to ask him only about what would benefit them of actual occurrences, and they did not ask him about hypothetical matters, puzzles, and the entangling of questions. Nor did they busy themselves with deriving and multiplying questions. Rather, their aspirations were confined to carrying out what he commanded them. When a matter befell them, they asked about it and he answered them. Allah, Exalted, has said: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 101]. ﴿A people before you asked such questions, and then they became disbelievers because of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 102].

There is a difference of opinion about these matters which were asked about: are they decreed matters (ahkam qadariyyah) or legislated rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah)? There are two views. It has been said that they are legislated rulings, and that "Allah has pardoned them" means He remained silent about their prohibition. Thus their asking about them was the cause of their being prohibited; had they not asked, they would have remained pardoned. From this is the Prophet's ﷺ saying, when he was asked about Hajj: "Is it every year?" He said: "If I said yes, it would have become obligatory. Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their many questions and their disputing with their prophets." The Hadith of Abu Tha'labah mentioned above, "Indeed the greatest of the Muslims in crime against the Muslims," also indicates this interpretation. Another Hadith is also of this kind: "Allah has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has remained silent about things out of mercy, not forgetfulness, so do not search for them." It has also been explained as referring to their asking about some decreed matters, such as the statement of 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah: "Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" and another's statement: "Where is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "In the Fire."

The correct view is that the verse covers the prohibition of both types. On this basis, Allah's words ﴿if they were made known to you, would distress you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 101] apply in matters of creation and decree: it distresses them that something they dislike should become apparent to them from what they asked about. And in matters of legal obligation (taklif), it distresses them that something should become apparent to them whose burden of obligation would be hard for them from what they asked about. As for Allah's words ﴿But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known to you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 101], there are two views:

The first: If the Qur'an descends concerning them initially, without a question, and then you ask about their details and knowledge, they will be made known and explained to you. The meaning of "the time of revelation" here is the period immediately connected with it, not the exact moment of descent. It seems that this is a permission for them to ask about the details of what was revealed and to know it after its revelation. Thus it removes the presumption that questioning about things is prohibited absolutely.

The second view is that it is a matter of threat and warning. That is: if you ask about these things during the time of revelation, the explanation of what you asked about will come to you with what will distress you. The meaning is: do not expose yourselves to asking about what its explanation would distress you. And if you do expose yourselves to it during the time of revelation, it will be made known to you.

His words ﴿Allah has pardoned them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 101] mean: He has pardoned their explanation, both as news and as a command. Rather, its explanation has been concealed from you out of mercy, forgiveness, and forbearance. Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing. On the first view, Allah has pardoned the obligation to them, as a widening (of ease) upon you. On the second view, Allah has pardoned their explanation, so that it does not distress you.

His words ﴿A people before you asked such questions, and then they became disbelievers because of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 102] intend the category of those questions, not their specific instances. That is: a people before you exposed themselves to similar questions, and when their explanations were made known to them, they disbelieved in them. So beware of resembling them and of exposing yourselves to what they exposed themselves to.

The ruling of this verse has not ceased. Rather, it is not befitting for a servant to expose himself to asking about what, if it became apparent to him, would distress him. Rather, he should seek to be spared as much as he can, and take hold of Allah's pardon. From here 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said, when his companion asked him about his water, whether it was pure or not: "O owner of the water-spout, do not inform us." Likewise, it is not befitting for a servant to ask his Lord to reveal to him from his circumstances and his end what He has concealed and veiled from him, for it may distress him if it were revealed to him. So asking about all of that is exposing oneself to what Allah dislikes, for He, glory be to Him, dislikes its disclosure, and that is why He remained silent about it. And Allah knows best.

(Section)

They said: Whoever reflects on the reports narrated in condemnation of opinion (ra'y) will find that they do not go beyond these disapproved categories. We will mention the reports of the Successors (tabi'un) and those after them on this matter, so that their intent may become clear. Al-Khushani said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "May Allah curse 'Did you see?'"

Yahya ibn Sa'id said: Salih ibn Muslim also narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Sha'bi about a matter concerning marriage, and he said: "If I inform you of my opinion, then urinate upon it."

They said: This is the statement of al-Sha'bi regarding his opinion, and he is one of the great Successors. He met one hundred and twenty of the Companions and took knowledge from most of them.

Al-Tahawi said: Sulayman ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid narrated to us, Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Whatever these ones among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have brought to you, take it; and whatever is of their opinion, throw it into the latrine (al-hushsh)."

Al-Bukhari said: Sunayd ibn Dawud narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Zayd, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who said: It was said to Jabir ibn Zayd: "They are writing down what they hear from you." He said: "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un (indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return). They write it down, and I will retract it tomorrow."

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: Ijtihad of opinion (ijtihad al-ra'y) is consulting the people of knowledge, not that one says it by his own opinion.

Ibn Abi Khaythamah said: al-Hawti narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Sawadah ibn Ziyad and 'Amr ibn al-Muhajir, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, that he wrote to the people: "There is no opinion for anyone in the presence of a Sunnah which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established."

Abu Basirah said: I heard Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say to al-Hasan al-Basri: "It has reached me that you give fatwas by your opinion. So do not give a fatwa by your opinion unless it is a Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Mahbub narrated to me, 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, Ibn al-Zibriqan ibn 'Abd Allah al-Usaydi narrated to us, that Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah said: "Beware of sitting with one who says: 'Did you see? Did you see?'"

Aban ibn 'Isa ibn Dinar narrated, from his father, from Ibn al-Qasim, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, who said: "Leave the Sunnah to proceed; do not confront it with opinion."

Yunus narrated from Abu al-Aswad, who is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, who said: I heard 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr say: "The affair of the Children of Israel remained balanced until there arose among them the mawaliyun (those born of captive mothers from the nations), who took up opinion among them, and so they misled them."

Ibn Wahb mentioned, from Ibn Shihab, that he said, while mentioning what people had fallen into of this opinion and their abandonment of the Sunnahs: "The Jews and Christians only stripped themselves of the knowledge they had in their hands when they followed opinion and engaged in it."

Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me that a man asked Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar about something, and he said: "I have not heard anything about this." The man said to him: "Then inform me, may Allah set you right, by your opinion." He said: "No." He repeated it to him, and he said: "I am content with your opinion." Salim said: "Indeed I am (a person who), if I inform you of my opinion, then you go and afterward I form another opinion, and I will not find you."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah al-Uwaysi narrated to us, Malik ibn Anas narrated to us, who said: Rabi'ah used to say to Ibn Shihab: "My situation is not like your situation. I give my opinion; whoever wishes takes it and acts upon it, and whoever wishes leaves it."

Al-Firyabi said: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us, who said: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi say: I heard Hammad ibn Zayd say: It was said to Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani: "Why do you not look into opinion?" Ayyub said: "It was said to the donkey: 'Why do you not chew the cud?' He said: 'I dislike chewing falsehood.'"

Al-Firyabi said: al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid narrated to us, my father informed me, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: "Hold to the narrations of those who preceded you, even if the people abandon you; and beware of the opinions of men, even if they embellish speech for you."

Abu Zur'ah said: Abu Mushir narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, when asked, would not answer until he said: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (there is no power nor strength except with Allah). This is opinion, and opinion may err or be correct."

Abu Yusuf and al-Hasan ibn Ziyad both narrated from Abu Hanifah that he said: "This knowledge of ours is opinion, and it is the best that we have been able to attain. Whoever brings us something better than it, we will accept it from him."

Al-Tahawi said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, Ashhab ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, who said: I was with Malik when he was asked about al-battah (an irrevocable divorce). I took my tablets to write down what he said, and Malik said to me: "Do not do that, for perhaps in the evening I will say that it is a single (revocable) divorce."

Ma'n ibn 'Isa al-Qazzaz said: I heard Malik say: "I am only a human being; I err and I am correct. So look into my statements: whatever agrees with the Book and the Sunnah, take it; and whatever does not agree with the Book and the Sunnah, leave it." May Allah be pleased with the Imams of Islam, and reward them well for their counsel. The people of knowledge and religion among their followers have indeed complied with their advice and followed their path.

(Section)

His saying, may He be exalted, relating about His intimate friend Ibrahim that he said: ﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [makes] from my descendants [such]﴾

And His saying: ﴿So make hearts among the people incline toward them﴾

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy and monasticism﴾

And His saying, relating about Zakariyya that he said about his son: ﴿And make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾

And He said concerning the other side: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard﴾

And He said: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾

These coverings and deafness are the intensity of hatred, aversion and turning away, by which they are unable to hear or understand. The verification is that this arises from the coverings and deafness; it necessitates it and is its requirement.

So whoever interprets the coverings and deafness by it has interpreted them by their necessitated and required effect. In any case, that aversion, turning away and hatred are among their actions, and they are made by Allah, glorified is He, just as compassion, mercy, and the inclination of hearts toward His House are among their actions, and Allah is the One who makes them. He is the Maker of essences, their attributes, actions, wills and beliefs, so all of that is made and created by Him, even though the servant is the doer of it by his choice and will.

If it is said: all of this is contradicted by His saying: ﴿Allah did not make any bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾

And the bahirah and sa'ibah only became so by the making of the servants, so He informed that this was not by His making?

It is said: there is no contradiction, praise be to Allah, between the texts of the Book in any way. The "making" here is legislative and commanding, not existential and decreed. For making in the Book of Allah is divided into these two types, just as command, permission, decree, prescription and prohibition are divided into them, as its explanation will come, God willing. So He, glorified is He, negated from the bahirah and sa'ibah His religious, legislative making, meaning that He did not legislate that nor command it; rather, those who disbelieved fabricated lies against Him and made that a religion for Him without knowledge.

Among this is His saying: ﴿So that He may make what Satan throws a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened﴾

So He informed that this trial resulting from what Satan threw was by His making, glorified is He, and this is existential, decreed making. Among this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih: "O Allah, make me for You grateful, for You remembering, for You fearing, for You obedient, for You humble, for You a sorrowful penitent (awwah munib)," so he asked his Lord to make him so. All of these are voluntary actions occurring by the servant's will and choice. And in this hadith: "and make my tongue firm (wa saddid lisani)," and making the tongue firm means making it speak what is right (al-sadad) of speech. Similar is his saying in another hadith: "O Allah, make me sincere to You (mukhlisan)." Similar is his saying: "O Allah, make me the greatest of Your thankfulness, the most abundant of Your remembrance, the one who follows Your advice most, and who best preserves Your command."

Similar is the saying of the believers: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and make firm our feet﴾. So patience and the firmness of feet are two voluntary acts, but the granting of patience and the making firm is the act of the Lord, exalted is He, and it is Him who is asked; while patience and steadfastness are their act, subsisting in them in reality.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 5, verse 105 (part 1 of 2):

Abu Tha'labah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the words of the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, take care of yourselves; the one who has gone astray cannot harm you if you are guided﴾. The verse was mentioned.

He said: "Enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, until you see stinginess obeyed, desire followed, the world preferred, and every person of opinion pleased with his own opinion. Then you must attend to yourself and leave the common people alone, for behind you are days in which patience will be like grasping a live coal. Whoever acts in them will have the reward of fifty men who act like your actions." Related by Abu Dawud.

When a believer whom Allah has granted insight (basirah) into his religion, understanding (fiqh) of the Sunnah of His Messenger, and comprehension of His Book, and has shown him what people are engaged in of desires, innovations (bid'ah) and misguidance, and their turning away from the Straight Path upon which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions were, then if he wishes to take this path, he must prepare himself to bear the reviling of the ignorant and the people of innovation, their attacks on him, their disparagement of him, their turning people away from him and their warning people against him. This is what their predecessors among the disbelievers did with the one they followed, their leader (ﷺ). But if he calls them to that and criticises what they are upon, then their uproar will rise, they will seek to harm him, set snares for him, and bring against him their cavalry and their infantry, both great and small.

He is a stranger in his religion, because their religions are corrupt; a stranger in his adherence to the Sunnah, because of their adherence to innovations; a stranger in his creed, because their creeds are corrupt; a stranger in his prayer, because of the badness of their prayer; a stranger in his path, because of the misguidance and corruption of their paths; a stranger in his lineage, because of the difference between his lineage and theirs; a stranger in his companionship with them, because he keeps company with them in ways their souls do not desire.

In sum, he is a stranger in the affairs of his worldly life and his hereafter. He finds from the common people no helper or supporter. He is a scholar among ignorant people, a holder of the Sunnah among people of innovation, a caller to Allah and His Messenger among callers to desires and innovations, one who enjoins good and forbids evil among a people for whom good is evil and evil is good.

(Section)

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned from Abu 'Imran, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent two angels to a village, saying: "Destroy it and its people." They found a man standing in prayer in a mosque, and they said: "O Lord, among them is Your servant so-and-so, who is praying." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Destroy it, and destroy him along with them, for his face has never changed (in anger) for My sake even once."

Al-Humaydi mentioned from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, who said: Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to me from Mis'ar: "An angel was commanded to cause a village to be swallowed up, and he said: 'O Lord, among them is so-and-so, the worshipper.' Allah revealed to him: 'Begin with him, for his face has never changed for My sake for a single hour.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When David committed the sin, he said: "O Lord, forgive me." He said: "I have forgiven you, and I have imposed its shame upon the Children of Israel." He said: "O Lord, how can that be, when You are the Just Judge who wrongs no one? I commit the sin, and You impose its shame upon others." So Allah revealed to him: "When you committed the sin, they did not hasten to condemn you."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Anas ibn Malik that he entered upon 'A'ishah, together with another man. The man said to her: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about earthquakes." She said: "When they make adultery lawful, drink wine, and play musical instruments, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, becomes jealous in His heaven and says to the earth: 'Shake with them.' If they repent and desist, well and good; otherwise He will collapse it upon them." He said: "O Mother of the Believers, is that a punishment for them?" She said: "Yes, an admonition and a mercy for the believers, and a deterrent, punishment and wrath upon the disbelievers." Anas said: "I have not heard a hadith after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that delighted me more than this hadith."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned a mursal hadith (one whose chain is missing a Companion): "The earth shook during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he placed his hand upon it and said: 'Be still, for your time has not yet come.' Then he turned to his Companions and said: 'Your Lord wants you to seek His pleasure, so seek His pleasure.' Then the people were shaken during the time of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: 'O people, this earthquake is only because of something you have introduced. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if it returns I will never dwell among you in it again.'"

In the Manaqib of 'Umar by Ibn Abi al-Dunya: "The earth shook during the time of 'Umar, so he struck it with his hand and said: 'What is wrong with you? What is wrong with you? Indeed, if it were the Resurrection, it would tell its news. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: On the Day of Resurrection, there will be no cubit nor span of it but that it will speak.'"

Imam Ahmad mentioned from Safiyyah, who said: Medina was shaken during the time of 'Umar, and he said: "O people, what is this? How quickly you have innovated! If it returns, I will not dwell among you in it."

Ka'b said: The earth only shakes when sins are committed upon it, and it trembles in fear of the Lord, may His majesty be exalted, lest He look upon it.

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote to the provinces: "To proceed: this tremor is something by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, rebukes His servants. I have written to the provinces that they should go out on such-and-such a day of such-and-such a month, and whoever has anything should give it in charity, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿He has indeed succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ [al-A'la: 14-15]."

And say as Adam said: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-A'raf: 23].

And say as Noah said: ﴿And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers﴾ [Hud: 47].

And say as Jonah said: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87].

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When people hoard dinars and dirhams, deal in 'inah (a form of riba-based sale), follow the tails of cows, and abandon jihad in the way of Allah, Allah will send upon them a calamity that He will not lift from them until they return to their religion." Related by Abu Dawud with a good chain.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, who said: "We have seen a time when no one was more entitled to his dinar and dirham than his Muslim brother." And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When people hoard dinars and dirhams, deal in 'inah, abandon jihad in the way of Allah, and take the tails of cows, Allah will send down upon them a calamity from the sky, and He will not lift it from them until they return to their religion."

Al-Hasan said: By Allah, the trial (fitnah) is nothing but a punishment from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon people.

One of the prophets of the Children of Israel looked at what Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) was doing to them and said: "Because of what our hands have earned, You have empowered over us one who does not know You and does not show us mercy."

Bukhtnassar said to Daniel: "What empowered me over your people?" He said: "The enormity of your sin and the wrongdoing of my people against themselves."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from the hadith of 'Ammar ibn Yasir and Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that "when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wants to inflict vengeance upon His servants, He causes the children to die and wombs of women to become barren, so the punishment descends, and among them there is no one shown mercy."

He mentioned from Malik ibn Dinar, who said: I read in the wisdom literature: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I am Allah, the King of kings; the hearts of kings are in My hands. Whoever obeys Me, I make them a mercy upon him, and whoever disobeys Me, I make them a punishment upon him. So do not occupy yourselves with reviling the kings, but turn to Me, and I will incline them toward you."

In the mursal reports of al-Hasan: "When Allah wants good for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their forbearing ones, and makes their governance subject to their generous ones. And when Allah wants evil for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their foolish ones, and makes their governance subject to their stingy ones."

Imam Ahmad and others mentioned from Qatadah, who said: Moses said: "O Lord, You are in the heavens and we are on the earth; what is the sign of Your anger from Your pleasure?" He said: "When I appoint over you your best, that is a sign of My pleasure with you, and when I appoint over you your worst, that is a sign of My wrath upon you."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, who said: Allah revealed to some prophets: "When one who knows Me disobeys Me, I will empower over him one who does not know Me."

He also mentioned from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the Hour will not come until Allah sends rulers who are liars, ministers who are sinners, helpers who are traitors, leaders who are oppressors, and reciters who are wicked. Their appearance is the appearance of monks, but their hearts are more putrid than carrion, and their desires are divided. Then Allah will bring upon them a dark and gloomy trial, and they will perish in it. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, Islam will be unraveled strand by strand, until no one says 'Allah, Allah.' You must enjoin good and forbid evil, or Allah will set over you your worst, who will inflict on you a terrible punishment. Then your best will supplicate, but their supplication will not be answered. You must enjoin good and forbid evil, or Allah will send against you one who has no mercy for your young and does not honour your old."

In the Mu'jam of al-Tabarani and others, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people cheat in measure or diminish the balance except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, withholds rain from them. Adultery does not spread among a people except that death spreads among them. Usury does not spread among a people except that Allah empowers madness over them. Killing does not spread among a people, with some of them killing others, except that Allah empowers their enemy over them. The deed of the people of Lot does not appear among a people except that sinking (of land) appears among them. And no people abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil except that their deeds are not raised and their supplications are not heard." Ibn Abi al-Dunya also related it from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, from his father, from Sa'id, with the same wording.

In the Musnad and others, from the hadith of 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me while his breathing was labored, and I recognised in his face that something had troubled him. He did not speak until he had performed ablution and went out. I pressed myself against the chamber. He ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to you: Enjoin good and forbid evil before you call upon Me and I do not answer you, and ask My help and I do not help you, and ask Me and I do not give to you.'"

Al-'Umari the ascetic said: Among your heedlessness of yourself and your turning away from Allah is that you see what angers Allah, yet you pass it by without commanding or forbidding it, out of fear of one who has no power to harm or benefit himself.

He also said: Whoever abandons enjoining good and forbidding evil out of fear of created beings, obedience will be removed from him; and if he commanded his child or some of his clients, they would make light of his right.

Imam Ahmad mentioned in his Musnad, from the hadith of Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "O people, you recite this verse, but you place it in other than its proper place: ﴿O you who believe, take care of yourselves; the one who has gone astray cannot harm you if you are guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105]. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'When people see a wrongdoer and do not restrain his hands, (in another wording: when they see evil and do not change it), Allah is about to envelop them all with punishment from Him.'"

Al-Awza'i mentioned from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When sin is hidden, it harms only its doer; but when it is made public and not changed, it harms the common people."

Imam Ahmad mentioned from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "The villages are about to be ruined while they are still inhabited." It was said: "How can they be ruined while they are inhabited?" He said: "When their wicked rise above their righteous, and their hypocrites lead the tribe."

Al-Awza'i mentioned from Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The worst of my Ummah will prevail over its best, until the believer hides among them as the hypocrite hides among us today."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from Ibn Abbas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There will come a time when the heart of the believer will melt as salt melts in water." It was asked: "Why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Because of the evil he sees, which he is unable to change."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Jarir that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no people among whom sins are committed while they are more honored and more numerous than those who commit them, and who do not change it, except that Allah will overtake them all with a punishment."
